<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 12"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Chain Reaction](/Feats.aspx?ID=3279) <actions string="Three Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 143

**Archetype** [Unexpected Sharpshooter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=123)

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

**Prerequisites**
[Unexpected Sharpshooter Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3272)

</column>

---

You fire your gun once, creating a devastating and unpredictable chain of events; perhaps your bullet strikes exactly the right spot on a water tower, causing it to flood and incite a stampede of horses which knock over a lantern that sets a city on fire. Whatever the exact chain reaction, and no matter how improbable, the indiscriminate catastrophe creates significant challenges for your enemies across a wide area while leaving everyone else alone.

 Make a Strike with a ranged weapon, and if you hit, you can make another Strike at a target within 30 feet of the first target. If you hit the second target, attempt to Strike a third target within 30 feet of the second target, and so on, continuing until you miss a target. You can cease the chain at any point; otherwise, it ends when you first miss an attack. However, you can't target the same creature more than once; each time you move to a new target, it must be a target you haven't made a Strike against yet during this particular use of Chain Reaction.

 This damage is caused by some improbable set of events that injures one target after another, rather than from actually making several shots. Perhaps you shot at a tree branch that then fell on the targets, or one target's scream caused another to accidentally set off their gun and shoot themselves in the foot. This means that only the first target suffers any special effects tied to the bullet (if it was magical ammunition, for example), but each target you hit still takes the same damage dealt by your Strike. Normally, all damage is of the same damage type as the initial bullet. However, the GM might choose to change the damage type based on their description of the chain reaction. For example, if one target was burned by fire, that target might take fire damage instead of physical damage.
name: Chain Reaction

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Dwarf" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=54" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Guns & Gears](/Sources.aspx?ID=98) pg. 201

**Access**
You are from Dongun Hold or Alkenstar.

</column>

---

Your family's traditions of defending against Geb's [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) have granted you a sixth sense for detecting spirits, haunts, and other restless dead, no matter their form or the strength of their presence. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to [Sense Motive](/Actions.aspx?ID=85) when trying to determine if a creature is possessed or under the influence of an effect that would make them [controlled](/Conditions.aspx?ID=6), a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks made to see through disguises worn by undead, and a +2 circumstance bonus when using the Seek action to find [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) [haunts](/Traits.aspx?ID=88) or undead within 30 feet of you.

 If you aren't using the [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) action or searching, the GM automatically rolls a [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=142) check for you to notice haunts or undead within 30 feet anyway. This check doesn't gain the usual +2 circumstance bonus, and instead takes a –2 circumstance penalty.
name: Scrutinizing Gaze

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Vigilante" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=326" />

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Gray Gardener](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=124)

**Prerequisites**
[Vigilante Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2083); member of the Gray Gardeners

</column>

---

Choose one creature you can see, and loudly declare the creature's life forfeit by your judgment. That creature becomes your condemned foe until they are defeated, you use Harsh Judgment on a different creature, or the encounter ends. You gain a +2 circumstance bonus to Perception checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) your condemned foe and on Intimidation checks to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) them. You have a –1 circumstance penalty to Perception checks to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) creatures other than your condemned foe and on Intimidation checks to [Demoralize](/Actions.aspx?ID=53) anyone other than your condemned foe. You typically can use Harsh Judgment only during an encounter, and if you try to use it to declare someone's life forfeit during exploration or downtime, you are likely to start an encounter.

<title level="2">Harsh Judgment leads to...</title>
[Accurate Swing](/Feats.aspx?ID=3334), [Execution](/Feats.aspx?ID=3338), [Frightful Condemnation](/Feats.aspx?ID=3333)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

The common folk heed your demands, and though your true foes rarely bend to your commands, when they do the hesitation can cost them the battle. You can cast [_command_](/Spells.aspx?ID=45) once every 10 minutes as a 1st-level occult innate spell. 

If you're in your vigilante identity, you can command the target only to approach you, drop prone, or stand in place. If you're in your social identity, you can command the target only to run away or release what the target is holding.

[Execution](/Feats.aspx?ID=3338) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Vigilante" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=326" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Night of the Gray Death](/Sources.aspx?ID=99) pg. 65

**Archetype** [Gray Gardener](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=124)

**Prerequisites**
[Harsh Judgment](/Feats.aspx?ID=3330); [Vigilante Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=2083); member of the Gray Gardeners

**Requirements**
You have condemned a foe with [Harsh Judgment.](/Feats.aspx?ID=3330)

</column>

---

You swing wide, attempting to behead your condemned foe. Make a melee Strike against your condemned foe. If you hit, your condemned foe takes 8d6 extra precision damage with a basic Fortitude save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. If the condemned foe is reduced to 0 Hit Points by the execution and requires a head to live, they die. For creatures with multiple heads, this usually kills the creature only if you sever its last head. The creature then becomes temporarily immune to your Execution for 1 day.

prerequisite: Harsh Judgment; Vigilante Dedication; member of the Gray Gardeners

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 1"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Harmless Doll](/Feats.aspx?ID=3340) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Poppet" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=418" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 63

</column>

---

You look like nothing more than an ordinary toy, doll, or statuette, and you can fool others with your innocuous appearance. You gain the trained proficiency rank in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) (or another skill if you're already trained in Deception), and you can [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) an inanimate toy or a mindless poppet. You can [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62) without any [cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=459) or [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4) from creatures that don't realize you're alive, so long as you're in a location where a toy of your shape wouldn't be out of place, like a carnival booth, city street, or toy shop (at the GM's discretion). If you succeed, onlookers still see you, but they mistake you for an inanimate toy. After being fooled once, they realize you're alive, and you can't Hide from them in that way again.
name: Harmless Doll

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 120

**Archetype** [Captivator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=125)

**Prerequisites**
Charisma 14; Trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) or Trained in [Diplomacy](/Skills.aspx?ID=6)

</column>

---

Your ability to captivate others borders on the preternatural. You are seldom at a loss in social situations, and you can create minor [enchantments](/Traits.aspx?ID=61) or [illusions](/Traits.aspx?ID=92). Choose Deception or Diplomacy. You become trained in that skill, or become an expert if you were already trained.

 Choose two cantrips from the [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3) list; each cantrip must be from either the enchantment or illusion school. You gain access to the Cast a Spell activity and can cast these spells as occult innate spells. You're trained in occult spell attack rolls and spell DCs. If you have a hand free, you can usually replace material components with somatic components, so you don't need to use a spell [component pouch](/Equipment.aspx?ID=33). Your key spellcasting ability for these spells is Charisma.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the captivator archetype.

<title level="2">Captivator Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Captivator Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=3359), [Effortless Captivation](/Feats.aspx?ID=3365), [Heightened Captivation](/Feats.aspx?ID=3362), [Look Again](/Feats.aspx?ID=3367), [Reactive Charm](/Feats.aspx?ID=3364)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 121

**Archetype** [Captivator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=125)

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Captivator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3358)

**Trigger**
You are the target of a spell or attack.

</column>

---

You're so charming and distracting that when pressed, you can cast a simple enchantment in time to foil an attacker. You cast any of your 1st-level [enchantment](/Traits.aspx?ID=61) spells that normally take two actions or fewer to cast. This takes effect before the triggering spell or attack, and if the attacker is affected by your spell, it can make different decisions based on the effects (for instance, if you [_charm_](/Spells.aspx?ID=34) the attacker and it becomes [friendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=18) to you, it can choose a different target than you for its attack or spell). The attacking creature must be in range of your chosen spell, and if your spell requires targets, the attacking creature must be a valid target. Your spell affects only the attacking creature, even if it would normally affect more targets or an area.
name: Reactive Charm

</title>

<traits>

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
[Captivator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3358)

</column>

---

If your [illusions](/Traits.aspx?ID=92) or [enchantments](/Traits.aspx?ID=61) fail to ensnare the minds of others, you can cast them again. If your next action is to cast an innate enchantment or illusion spell and it fails to affect any targets, you do not lose the spell. You must use the same number of actions to recast the same spell on your following turn; if you can't, or choose not to, you waste that number of actions with no effect. After this second casting, you lose the spell whether it affected any targets or not. Look Again works only with spells that require targets and doesn't do anything if you cast a targeted spell but didn't select any targets.

</column>

---

Your experience with magic and its traditions lets you specialize in the casting of certain spells, customizing familiar spells to create novel effects. Whenever you gain a feat from this archetype, you either learn to modify the effects of a single spell, or you change one of the modifications from a previous feat. Each time you Cast the Spell corresponding to the feat you chose, you decide whether to cast its normal or modified version. You can only apply one modification to a spell at a time, even if you know more than one modification for that spell. Besides modifications mentioned in the feat, the spell functions as normal.

 Choose up to two 4th-level spell trickster archetype feats for which you meet the spell-casting prerequisite. You gain those feats, ignoring their level prerequisite.

**Special** You can’t select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the spell trickster archetype. The two feats you gain from taking the dedication don’t count toward this total.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 123

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_sigil_](/Spells.aspx?ID=286)

</column>

---

When you cast _sigil_, you can modify the spell to add the following to its standard effects: The target leaves a magical trail that you and others can try to follow. You and other creatures can attempt to [Track](/Actions.aspx?ID=66) the target, substituting an [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) check (whichever matches the magical tradition of your sigil spell) for the [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) check. Much like Tracking with Survival, this must take place somewhere the target has been and follow the trail; it doesn't allow anyone to find the target from a distance. You can only have a single target marked with a modified sigil in this way. If you use this ability again on a second target, the _sigil_ spell on the first target ends, and your mark fades.

<title level="2">Tracing Sigil leads to...</title>
[Beacon Mark](/Feats.aspx?ID=3383)
name: Tracing Sigil
prerequisite: Spell Trickster Dedication; ability to cast _sigil_

When you cast _sigil_, you can modify the spell to add the following heightened entry.

While the spell lasts, you can spend a single action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [detection](/Traits.aspx?ID=43), and [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47) traits, to attempt to locate the target, learning the direction to the target as long as you are within 1 mile of it. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 124

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Agile Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=3369); [Pickpocket](/Feats.aspx?ID=818)

</column>

---

When you cast [_mage hand_](/Spells.aspx?ID=177), you can remove its duration, modify its range to 20 feet, and modify its target to be an attended object within the spell's Bulk limit that wouldn't be time-consuming to remove. Add the following to the spell's standard effects: If the creature attending the object is willing to have you take the item, _mage hand_ carries the item to you. If the creature is unwilling, you must attempt to [Steal](/Actions.aspx?ID=68) the target object with a [Thievery](/Skills.aspx?ID=17) check. The usual restrictions on attempts to Steal an object apply, including the restrictions that you can't steal objects that would be extremely noticeable or time-consuming to remove (like worn shoes or armor or actively wielded objects) and you can't Steal from a creature in combat or otherwise on guard. On a successful Steal check, the _mage hand_ carries the item to you, and on a critical failure, you can't use this modification again for 1 hour. If you're a master in Thievery, you can attempt to Steal from a creature in combat or otherwise on guard, though if you do so, the spell's casting time increases by 1 action.
name: Larcenous Hand

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 10"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Toppling Tentacles](/Feats.aspx?ID=3391) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 125

**Archetype** [Spell Trickster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=126)

**Prerequisites**
[Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_black tentacles_](/Spells.aspx?ID=23)

</column>

---

When you cast _black tentacles_, replace the spell's standard effects with the following: Tentacles slither along the ground in the area, attempting to hinder anyone within. Sticky black tentacles attempt to [Trip](/Actions.aspx?ID=40) each creature in the area. Attempt spell attack rolls against the Reflex DCs of each affected creature. Any creature you succeed against is knocked [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) and takes 3d6 bludgeoning damage. Whenever a creature ends its turn in the area, the tentacles attempt to Trip that creature if it isn't already prone, and they deal 1d6 bludgeoning damage to any creature already prone. Creatures treat the spell's area as difficult terrain.
name: Toppling Tentacles
prerequisite: Spell Trickster Dedication; ability to cast _black tentacles_
prerequisite_markdown: [Spell Trickster Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3368); ability to cast [_black tentacles_](/Spells.aspx?ID=23)

>
[Wrestler Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3394) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 126

**Archetype** [Wrestler](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=127)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3); trained in [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attacks, and unarmored defense

</column>

---

Your training in the wrestling arts has made you particularly adept at moving, striking, and grappling while unencumbered. You become an expert in Athletics and gain the [Titan Wrestler](/Feats.aspx?ID=854) skill feat. You don't take the –2 circumstance penalty for making a lethal attack with your [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188) unarmed attacks. In addition, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your Fortitude DC when resisting an opponent's attempts to [Grapple](/Actions.aspx?ID=35) you or [Swallow you Whole](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=35).

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the wrestler archetype.

<title level="2">Wrestler Dedication leads to...</title>
[Aerial Piledriver](/Feats.aspx?ID=3402), [Clinch Strike](/Feats.aspx?ID=3398), [Disengaging Twist](/Feats.aspx?ID=3395), [Elbow Breaker](/Feats.aspx?ID=3396), [Form Lock (Wrestler)](/Feats.aspx?ID=3405), [Inescapable Grasp](/Feats.aspx?ID=3404), [Running Tackle](/Feats.aspx?ID=3399), [Spinebreaker](/Feats.aspx?ID=3403), [Strangle](/Feats.aspx?ID=3400), [Submission Hold](/Feats.aspx?ID=3401), [Suplex](/Feats.aspx?ID=3397)
name: Wrestler Dedication
prerequisite: Trained in Athletics; trained in unarmed attacks, and unarmored defense

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Grand Bazaar](/Sources.aspx?ID=100) pg. 127

[Wrestler Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3394)

**Requirements**
You have a creature [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33).

</column>

---

You twist and squeeze the breath out of your foe. Make an [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) melee Strike against the creature you have grabbed or restrained. On a success, you gain a circumstance bonus to damage equal to the number of weapon damage dice and the target can barely speak until the start of your next turn or until it [Escapes](/Actions.aspx?ID=79), whichever comes first. While it can barely speak, the target can't vocalize above a hoarse whisper, and it must succeed at a DC 10 flat check or lose any action that requires speech. For an action requiring speech that is also a [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104) action, like Casting a Spell with somatic and verbal components, the target just rolls a single DC 10 flat check, rather than an additional DC 5 flat check for being grabbed.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Prerequisites**
[Wrestler Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3394)

Your grasp has a supernatural quality to it, preventing your foes from easily escaping—with or without magical assistance. If a creature you have grabbed attempts to use a [teleportation](/Traits.aspx?ID=156) spell or effect, it must succeed at a DC 15 flat check or the spell fails. If a creature you have grabbed attempts to [Escape](/Actions.aspx?ID=79) while under the effect of [_freedom of movement_](/Spells.aspx?ID=128), it must succeed at a DC 15 flat check or be forced to roll the Escape attempt normally, rather than automatically succeeding.

Your growing link to cloud dragons has granted you the ability to walk on clouds. Once per hour, you can cast [_air walk_](/Spells.aspx?ID=6) on yourself as an innate arcane spell, but only to walk on clouds or fog.

<title level="2">Bloodsalt Dragon Disciple Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #171: Hurricane's Howl](/Sources.aspx?ID=101) pg. 79

The following archetype feats are for the dragon disciple archetype. You must take the Dragon Disciple Dedication feat before selecting any of these feats, and you must select cloud dragon (which is associated with the electricity energy type) as the type of dragon you've studied. The feats below are dragon disciple archetype feats. By studying the ruins (see the AP for full details), you gain access to the dragon disciple archetype and to these feats

 If you have the [draconic sorcerer](/Bloodlines.aspx?ID=5) bloodline, you must choose cloud dragon as your dragon type. This choice affects the [_dragon breath_](/Spells.aspx?ID=499) and [_dragon claws_](/Spells.aspx?ID=500) bloodline spells and several of the feats below.

**Related Feats**: [Deflecting Cloud](/Feats.aspx?ID=3408), [Mighty Wings](/Feats.aspx?ID=3409), [Shape of the Cloud Dragon](/Feats.aspx?ID=3407)

<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monsters of Myth](/Sources.aspx?ID=107) pg. 10

**Archetype** [Pactbound Initiate](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=167)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10); [Erutaki](/Languages.aspx?ID=54) or [Giant](/Languages.aspx?ID=8) language, must have earned the trust of a saumen kar who initiates you into the archetype

</column>

---

You befriended one of the last saumen kar and were infused with a fraction of their power, granting you the potential to become a guardian of their ancient pact. You gain [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) resistance equal to half your level. You can [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62) and [Sneak](/Actions.aspx?ID=63) while it's snowing even lightly, even if it wouldn't be thick enough to normally grant [concealment](/Conditions.aspx?ID=4). Finally, all saumen kar can sense the mark of their pact upon you, and their attitude toward you is typically one step better than it would be otherwise ([hostile](/Conditions.aspx?ID=23) to [unfriendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=40), unfriendly to [indifferent](/Conditions.aspx?ID=25), etc.) Most saumen kar are unfriendly to outsiders; this would make them indifferent to you.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from the pactbound initiate archetype.

<title level="2">Pactbound Dedication leads to...</title>
[Crown of the Saumen Kar](/Feats.aspx?ID=3416), [Frostbite Runes](/Feats.aspx?ID=3417), [Ice Crafter](/Feats.aspx?ID=3415)

Your horns are in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group and have the [shove](/Traits.aspx?ID=193) and [trip](/Traits.aspx?ID=196) traits.

Thick tattoos, each one a rune fragment from the saumen kar's long-lost language spelling out their pact with their equally lost deity, cover your body and stretch across your limbs, torso, and face. You gain a +1 status bonus to saving throws against [evil](/Traits.aspx?ID=64) and [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117) spells and effects. You can sense the presence of evil [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) as a pervasive taste of oily corruption in the air; this is a [vague](/Rules.aspx?ID=413) sense that allows you to know when such a creature is within 60 feet of you, though you can't precisely pinpoint their location with this sense. As normal for a vague sense, it can be fooled, but undead might not realize they need to take precautions against it. This sense also extends to living creatures who have the [negative healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=42) ability, like [dhampir](/Ancestries.aspx?ID=23).

 You deal an additional 1 cold damage with all Strikes made with an ice-crafted weapon. If you have the [Crown of the Saumen Kar](/Feats.aspx?ID=3416) feat, you deal an additional 1 cold damage with your unarmed horns Strikes.

<traits>

once per day

</column>

---

You activate the runes on your body to create an icy prison around a Huge or smaller creature you can see within 60 feet. The prison is a sphere made of unmelting ice, just large enough to fit your target. The target, and any creatures sharing its space, must attempt a Reflex save, with a DC using the higher of your class DC and spell DC. A creature that fails becomes trapped inside the prison. If it succeeds, the creature is pushed outside the prison into a space of its choice. If the target shares its space with a gargantuan creature, the effect fails.

 The dome has AC 10, Hardness 20, and 40 Hit Points; it's immune to [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27), critical hits, and precision damage. The prison lasts until destroyed, until you use this ability to create a new prison, or until you die.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Monsters of Myth](/Sources.aspx?ID=107) pg. 11

**Archetype** [Pactbound Initiate](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=167)

**Prerequisites**
[Frostbite Runes](/Feats.aspx?ID=3417)

</column>

---

You become a hybrid of your ancestry and a saumen kar. Your size increases to Large, and your reach becomes 10 feet. Your [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) resistance increases to be equal to your level, and you gain [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) resistance equal to half your level.

 You also gain the Blizzard Evasion reaction.

 **Blizzard Evasion** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Frequency** once per day; **Trigger** You take 40 or more physical damage from a single attack; **Effect** You discorporate into a whirling blizzard for up to 3 rounds. During this time, you gain resistance 10 to physical damage and weakness 10 to [force](/Traits.aspx?ID=75) damage. You gain a fly speed of 40 feet, but the only action you can take is to [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=94). The first time each round you enter another creature's space while discorporated, or the first time a creature enters your space, that creature takes 4d8 cold damage and must succeed at a Fortitude saving throw against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher, or else be [stunned 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=36). At the start of your turn, you can end this effect as a free action.
name: Bound in Ice

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Quest for the Frozen Flame</spoilers>

<traits>

<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #175: Broken Tusk Moon](/Sources.aspx?ID=112) pg. 78

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16)

</column>

---

You know how to make the best and most efficient use of a hunted animal's carcass. Choose a Large or larger corpse of an [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=9) that died within the past day. While using Survival to [Subsist](/Actions.aspx?ID=27) near the carcass, you always receive enough food for yourself and one additional Medium creature, using up the meat from the carcass to do so. Since you're using all of the animal, others can't use the carcass's meat for any other purpose, including their own use of All of the Animal.

<title level="2">Skill Feats</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #175: Broken Tusk Moon](/Sources.aspx?ID=112) pg. 78

Characters can gain access to the following new skill feats throughout “Broken Tusk Moon.”

 **All of the Animal**: Head scout Wipa teaches this skill feat to characters who help her butcher an animal for meat, such as the moose at the beginning of the adventure or another animal slain throughout the course of the Broken Tusk following's journey.

 **Spirit Speaker**: Mammoth Lord Argakoa, also known as Argakoa the Songsinger, might teach a fraction of her tremendous skill to a young scout who joins her in song. 

**Tame Animal**: The young herd tender Imek has a natural way with animals. She is happy to teach what she knows to any characters who display a similar reverence toward living creatures, such as by peacefully resolving their encounter with the giant porcupine in Chapter 1 of this adventure. Although this feat is particularly useful to characters who want to recruit animal followers throughout the Quest for the Frozen Flame Adventure Path, it isn't strictly necessary for the party to succeed in their adventures. It can be a great boon to parties taking part in other quests, as well.

**Related Feats**: [Spirit Speaker](/Feats.aspx?ID=3423), [Tame Animal](/Feats.aspx?ID=3424)
name: All of the Animal

Using low chants, body language that shows respect, and special movements that demonstrate to the spirit that you are an ally, you glean information from a spirit before it departs. This is a 1-minute activity. You must begin the activity while adjacent to the body of an [animal](/Traits.aspx?ID=9) or [beast](/Traits.aspx?ID=20) that died within the last 1 minute. As part of the activity, you ask one simple question of the spirit. Attempt a Nature check at a DC determined by the GM (normally, this is the [appropriate DC for the level of the animal or beast](/Rules.aspx?ID=554) when it was alive). Regardless of the result of your check, the spirit immediately departs and can't be used for Spirit Speaker again. If the creature had the [confused](/Conditions.aspx?ID=5) or [frightened](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) condition when it died, you can't get a result better than a critical failure. Only one creature can use Spirit Speaker on a given dead animal, as the effort takes the spirit's full attention. **Critical Success** The spirit answers you truthfully. The spirit's answer is likely to be terse or cryptic compared to normal communication with an animal, and it can pertain only to things the creature directly experienced or considered important. The spirit doesn't remember anything that happened more than 1 day ago.
**Success** As critical success, but the spirit doesn't recall anything that happened more than 1 hour ago.
**Failure** The spirit doesn't answer you.
**Critical Failure** The spirit is wracked with misery or bewilderment and gives you an erroneous answer. Although this feat is particularly useful to characters who want to recruit animal followers throughout the Quest for the Frozen Flame Adventure Path, it isn't strictly necessary for the party to succeed in their adventures. It can be a great boon to parties taking part in other quests, as well. Related Feats : All of the Animal, Spirit Speaker

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Quest for the Frozen Flame</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #175: Broken Tusk Moon](/Sources.aspx?ID=112) pg. 81

**Archetype** [Game Hunter](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=169)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16)

</column>

---

You are skilled at tracking big game animals and similar creatures. You gain the [Hunt Prey](/Actions.aspx?ID=10) action, but you can designate only [animals](/Traits.aspx?ID=9), [beasts](/Traits.aspx?ID=20), and [dragons](/Traits.aspx?ID=50) as prey. In addition to the other benefits of Hunt Prey, you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) checks against your hunted prey.

 When you succeed at a Strike against your hunted prey while it's [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16), it must attempt a Fortitude save against your class DC. On a failure, the prey's Speeds are each reduced by 10 feet for 1 round; on a critical failure, the duration of this effect is 1 minute. The prey is then temporarily immune to this effect for 10 minutes.

 If you already have Hunt Prey, you become an expert in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16). You apply the Stealth bonus and the Speed reduction only when your prey is an animal, beast, or dragon.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the game hunter archetype.

<title level="2">Game Hunter Dedication leads to...</title>
[Big Game Trapper](/Feats.aspx?ID=3426), [Keep Pace](/Feats.aspx?ID=3427), [Quick Positioning](/Feats.aspx?ID=3428)

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #176: Lost Mammoth Valley](/Sources.aspx?ID=113) pg. 77

**Access**
Pine leshies have access to this feat

</column>

---

You rely on fire and extreme heat to sprout and regrow. Whenever you take fire damage, at the beginning of your next turn, you regain Hit Points equal to half your character level (minimum 1). The total number of Hit Points you recover in this way, including any adjustments that increase the effects of healing, can't exceed half the Hit Points you lost from the fire damage you took. For example, if an effect deals 15 fire damage and you have fire resistance 5, you would take 10 fire damage and Pyrophilic Recovery could recover at most 5 Hit Points, regardless of any other effects that increase healing. If you take fire damage more than once before your next turn, the Hit Points recovered from Pyrophilic Recovery are cumulative, though still no more than half the fire damage taken each time.
name: Pyrophilic Recovery

[Druid Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=701) or [Wizard Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=742)

</column>

---

Your mask carries the legacy of Verdant Spider, the Speaker of Needs, allowing you to deceive and outwit your foes. You can attempt to [Feint](/Actions.aspx?ID=48) a target from up to 30 feet away, and if you succeed or critically succeed in your Feint attempt, the target of your Feint takes a –2 circumstance penalty to saving throws against your spells until the start of your next turn. If you don't have the [Conceal Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=640) feat, you gain it as a bonus feat, allowing you to disguise your spellcasting from others' eyes. If you already have the Conceal Spell feat, you can use Conceal Spell once per round as a free action instead of as a single action.

<title level="2">Masks of the Magic Warriors</title>

**Source** [Pathfinder #174: Shadows of the Ancients](/Sources.aspx?ID=115) pg. 78

In becoming Jatembe's new Magic Warriors, the heroes have unlocked secrets of magical potential that none have reached since the earliest Ten Magic Warriors walked the plazas of the Magaambya.

 On reaching 20th level, the heroes should have the option of taking one of these archetype feats, based on the type of animal they chose for their mask when they first created it in _Pathfinder Adventure Path #169: Kindled Magic_. These options are each themed to one of Jatembe's magic warriors, but if a hero's mask doesn't fit with a specific animal from this list or the player feels their animal embodies a different effect from the list, feel free to reflavor the feat names to fit the hero's spirit face. For instance, the Cunning Trickster mask could easily be a rodent or a fox, not just a spider.

**Related Feats**: [Emancipator's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3434), [Grand Medic's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3435), [Protective Spirit Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3436), [Sky Master Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3437), [Stalking Feline Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3438), [Storyteller's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3439), [Thick Hide Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3440), [Tireless Guide's Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3441), [Vigilant Mask](/Feats.aspx?ID=3442)

Your mask carries the protective instincts of White Bull, the Horn Forger, and no one will hurt your allies while you have anything to say about it. Immediately after you Cast a non-cantrip Spell that targets only one ally, you can choose to have the spell also give that creature a +1 circumstance bonus to AC until the start of your next turn. You also gain the Protector's Interdiction reaction.

**Protector's Interdiction** <actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** An adjacent ally is hit or critically hit by an attack; **Effect** You interpose yourself between your ally and the attack. The attack hits you instead, or critically hits you if it critically hit your ally.

Your mask grants the extraordinary magical senses of Carmine Jaws, the Hyena who Looks Between. You gain [scent](/Rules.aspx?ID=417) as a [precise sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) to a range of 60 feet. If you already have scent as a precise sense, increase its range by 60 feet. You can sometimes catch a faint whiff of magic itself. Immediately after you Cast a non-cantrip Spell, your scent extends between worlds, like Carmine Jaws's own. This causes you to be able to smell [ethereal](/Traits.aspx?ID=63) creatures, those in an [extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67) space with an aperture that's within your scent range, [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) creatures and objects, and other creatures and objects that are insubstantial or not fully in phase with reality. Unlike your normal scent, this is an [imprecise sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=413).

You've undertaken the ultimate challenge of the Mammoth Lords and tamed a megafauna. You gain a megafauna you tamed as a [young animal companion](/Rules.aspx?ID=151). Your megafauna animal companion must be a megafauna appropriate to the Realm of the Mammoth Lords; see the What Counts as Megafauna? sidebar for guidance and examples. While an animal companion usually starts as Small, you can begin with a Medium version of that animal (changing no statistics other than its size).

 Contrary to the usual rules for animal companions, this feat can give you a second animal companion. If you have more than one animal companion, you can adventure with only one of them at a time. You can switch between them like a [beastmaster](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=50) does. You gain the Call Companion action, as the beastmaster archetype, and you follow all the other rules found in the Call Companion sidebar.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from this archetype.

<title level="2">Mammoth Lord Dedication leads to...</title>
[Gigantic Megafauna Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=3452), [Mammoth Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=3444), [Mature Megafauna Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=3445), [Megafauna Veterinarian](/Feats.aspx?ID=3446), [Specialized Megafauna Companion](/Feats.aspx?ID=3453), [Speech of the Mammoth Lords](/Feats.aspx?ID=3447), [Staggering Blow](/Feats.aspx?ID=3450), [Stalwart Mind](/Feats.aspx?ID=3449), [Unbreakable Bond](/Feats.aspx?ID=3451)

>
[Exorcist Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3454) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 22

**Archetype** [Exorcist](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=171)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) or Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)

</column>

---

You've learned to attract, quell, and purify spirits, housing them in a special receptacle called a _spirit dwelling_ until they're ready to move on. Through the power of prayers or ritual incantations, one mundane object in your possession becomes a _spirit dwelling_. Your _spirit dwelling_ functions as a lure for lost spirits weakened by their time on the [Material Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=1). Each day during your daily preparations, your _spirit dwelling_ attracts a spirit wisp who comes to dwell inside. If your _spirit dwelling_ contains no wisps, you can spend 10 minutes in a minor ritual to cast your _spirit dwelling_ around an area and attract another wisp. You can also capture stronger spirit remnants from vanquished [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) spirits, as explained in the [Spirit Dwellings and Remnants](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=171) sidebar. As long as your _spirit dwelling_ contains any spirits, it glows faintly, casting dim light in a 10-foot radius.

 As an exorcist, you do more than just collect spirits: you also help rid them of their burdens and lingering resentments, aiding their transition from the Material Plane. Every day, before your daily preparations, any spirit wisps and remnants remaining within your _spirit dwelling_ from the previous day are purified and can join the River of Souls in their final journey to [Pharasma's](/Deities.aspx?ID=14) [Boneyard](/Planes.aspx?ID=15).

 You can also learn abilities that let you purify a spirit in your _spirit dwelling_ immediately in a cathartic surge, granting you a helpful effect as they depart for the afterlife. Any actions you gain from the exorcist archetype gain either the [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48) or [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120) trait, depending on whether you used Occultism or Religion to qualify for Exorcist Dedication.

 Spirit's Mercy is the simplest of the purifications.

 **Spirit's Mercy** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117)) **Trigger** You take [positive](/Traits.aspx?ID=128) or [negative](/Traits.aspx?ID=118) damage, or you take any type of damage caused by a [haunt](/Traits.aspx?ID=88), [ghost](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=51), or other [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) undead; **Cost** 1 spirit wisp or remnant; **Effect** You purify a spirit by having it perform a final act of mercy to lessen the damage caused by another spirit. This grants you resistance to positive and negative damage (or resistance to all damage if caused by a haunt or incorporeal undead) against the triggering effect. If you expend a spirit wisp, the resistance is equal to twice your level. If you expend a spirit remnant, the resistance is equal to three times the level of the incorporeal undead or haunt from which you gained the remnant.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the exorcist archetype.

<title level="2">Exorcist Dedication leads to...</title>
[Cast Out](/Feats.aspx?ID=3455), [Enticing Dwelling](/Feats.aspx?ID=3458), [Spirit's Absolution](/Feats.aspx?ID=3456), [Spirit's Anguish](/Feats.aspx?ID=3457)
name: Exorcist Dedication
prerequisite: Trained in Occultism or Trained in Religion

Any actions you gain from the exorcist archetype gain either the divine or occult trait, depending on whether you used Occultism or Religion to qualify for Exorcist Dedication. Spirit's Mercy is the simplest of the purifications. Spirit's Mercy Reaction (necromancy) Trigger You take positive or negative damage, or you take any type of damage caused by a haunt, ghost, or other incorporeal undead; Cost 1 spirit wisp or remnant; Effect You purify a spirit by having it perform a final act of mercy to lessen the damage caused by another spirit. This grants you resistance to positive and negative damage (or resistance to all damage if caused by a haunt or incorporeal undead) against the triggering effect. If you expend a spirit wisp, the resistance is equal to twice your level. If you expend a spirit remnant, the resistance is equal to three times the level of the incorporeal undead or haunt from which you gained the remnant. Special You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the exorcist archetype. Exorcist Dedication leads to... Cast Out, Enticing Dwelling, Spirit's Absolution, Spirit's Anguish

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 24

**Archetype** [Hallowed Necromancer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=172)

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13); good alignment, able to cast spells using spell slots, able to cast at least one [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117) spell

</column>

---

You've studied techniques allowing you to blend so-called hallowed necromancy into your own spellcasting to bolster the living and destroy the [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160). You gain the [_hallowed ground_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1103) focus spell. It costs 1 Focus Point to cast a focus spell. This feat grants a focus pool of 1 Focus Point that you can recover using the [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) activity. You can Refocus by meditating or praying to connect yourself to conduits of positive energy. Focus spells from the hallowed necromancer archetype have the same tradition as your spell slots.

 Casting spells that create, heal, or otherwise aid or promote undead is anathema to you, as is cooperation with undead. Using negative energy isn't anathema, as it serves a natural purpose, but twisting that negative energy for creation is blasphemous to you. If you perform acts that are anathema to your principles, you lose access to all feats from this archetype. These abilities can be regained only with an [_atone_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=2) ritual.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the hallowed necromancer archetype.

<title level="2">Hallowed Necromancer Dedication leads to...</title>
[Advanced Hallowed Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=3463), [Consecrated Aura](/Feats.aspx?ID=3465), [Death Warden](/Feats.aspx?ID=3462), [Hallowed Initiate](/Feats.aspx?ID=3460), [Positive Luminance](/Feats.aspx?ID=3464), [Sacred Spells](/Feats.aspx?ID=3461)

Your body radiates positive energy, making your very presence disorienting to [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) and encouraging them to move away from you. The effect plays upon the instincts flowing through their bodies from negative energy and can thus affect even [mindless](/Traits.aspx?ID=108) creatures. You gain an aura of positive energy in a 20-foot emanation. Each undead creature that ends its turn in your aura must succeed at a Will save against your spell DC or become [frightened 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=19) (frightened 2 on a critical failure). A creature that succeeds at its save is temporarily immune for 1 minute.

**Special** Your aura gains the trait of the magical tradition for the spells you used to qualify for Hallowed Necromancer Dedication.

>
[Soul Warden Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3466) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 26

**Archetype** [Soul Warden](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=173)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) or Trained in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13); worships [Pharasma](/Deities.aspx?ID=14) or a psychopomp usher

</column>

---

You can take 10 minutes to emblazon Pharasma's holy sigil—a spiraling comet that represents the winding path a soul takes through its existence—upon a shield, tabard, banner, or other prominent object that your wear or wield. The symbol doesn't fade until 1 year has passed, but if you emblazon the symbol again, any symbol you previously emblazoned and any symbol already emblazoned on that item instantly disappears. The item becomes a [religious symbol](/Equipment.aspx?ID=41) of Pharasma and can be used as a divine focus while emblazoned.

 Whenever an [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) creature or captive soul is within 100 feet of this object, the spiral glows, shedding dim blue light in a 10-foot radius. If the creature is hiding or the soul is hidden, it must succeed at a [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) check against your Perception DC to fool the sigil and prevent the spiral from glowing.

 In addition, you can cast [_disrupt undead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=79) as a divine innate cantrip at will. As normal, a cantrip is automatically heightened to half your level rounded up. You gain access to the Cast a Spell activity if you didn't have it already. You're trained in divine spell attack rolls and spell DCs. Your key spellcasting ability for these spells is Wisdom.

 When you have at least two other feats from this archetype, the spiral glows with [bright light](/Rules.aspx?ID=407) in a 10-foot radius (and [dim light](/Rules.aspx?ID=408) for the next 10 feet). Feats that require a creature or object to be in the light of your spiral function whether it's in the bright or dim light.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the soul warden archetype.

<title level="2">Soul Warden Dedication leads to...</title>
[Cycle Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=3467), [Liberate Soul](/Feats.aspx?ID=3469), [Psychopomp Familiar](/Feats.aspx?ID=3468), [Safeguard Soul](/Feats.aspx?ID=3472), [Spiral Sworn](/Feats.aspx?ID=3470)
name: Soul Warden Dedication
prerequisite: Trained in Occultism or Trained in Religion; worships Pharasma or a psychopomp usher

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Archetype** [Undead Slayer](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=174)

**Prerequisites**
[Undead Slayer Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3474)

</column>

---

You establish a safe house where you can prepare for your hunt. The sanctum is roughly the size of a 20-foot cube. This sanctum is in a location you have access to and can be part of a larger structure, such as the basement of a temple or hidden room of a library. Setting up or moving your sanctum takes a week of downtime. Your sanctum protects objects and people inside it from magical detection and the prying eyes of [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160). This has the effects of [_nondetection_](/Spells.aspx?ID=209), using your [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) modifier for the [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) DC and half your level rounded up for the counteract level. Additionally, undead attempting to locate the entrance to your sanctum via mundane Perception must succeed against either your Religion DC or the normal DC to find the sanctum, whichever is higher.
name: Hunter's Sanctum

You've dedicated yourself to studying ancient techniques and memorized minor prayers against [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) to swiftly dispatch them. Make a Strike against a creature you know is undead. This counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty. If this Strike hits, you deal one extra die of positive damage, with the same die size as the weapon or [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack you used. Any further Strikes you make against the same creature before the start of your next turn using the same weapon or unarmed attack deal extra positive damage equal to the number of weapon dice. As normal, the positive damage harms only undead and creatures with [negative healing](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=42).

 If you're at least 10th level, increase this to two extra dice, and if you're at least 18th level, increase it to three extra dice.

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 33 **Archetype** [Reanimator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=175) (Level 12) **Prerequisites** ability to create or control [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160); [cleric](/Classes.aspx?ID=5) with a negative font, [oracle](/Classes.aspx?ID=14) of [bones](/Mysteries.aspx?ID=3), or [necromancer](/ArcaneSchools.aspx?ID=7) [wizard](/Classes.aspx?ID=12) --- Necromantic energy demonstrates your power over undead, creating a demeanor that commands their fear and respect. Undead creatures can immediately sense your Necromancer's Visage and tend to act accordingly. If you take a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300) against an undead creature, it becomes permanently immune to your Necromancer's Visage, and your Necromancer's Visage ends. You can spend 10 minutes to restore your Necromancer's Visage, though any creatures that became permanently immune remain so. Each time an undead creature 2 or more levels lower than you attacks you, it must attempt a Will save against your spell DC. If you're also affected by [_sanctuary_](/Spells.aspx?ID=266) or a similar effect, only one affects the attacker (you choose which).
**Critical Success** The creature is permanently immune to your Necromancer's Visage.
**Success** The creature can attempt its attack and any other attacks against you this turn.
**Failure** The creature can't attack you and wastes the action. It can't attempt further attacks against you this turn.
**Critical Failure** The creature wastes the action and can't attempt to attack you as long as your Necromancer's Visage persists. **Special** This feat has the trait matching your spellcasting tradition.

---

You repurpose the negative energy that flows through your minions at a moment's notice. Instantly destroy one undead minion within 60 feet that is permanently under your control. If your next action is to cast a [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117) spell from a spell slot, you don't expend the slot. The spell's level must be half the destroyed minion's level or lower and the spell can't have a duration.

**Special** This feat has the trait matching your spellcasting tradition.

>
[Reanimator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3486) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 34

**Archetype** [Reanimator](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=175)

**Prerequisites**
able to cast [_animate dead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=666) with a spell slot

</column>

---

You have dedicated your studies to the art of raising and commanding undead. If you're a spontaneous spellcaster with _animate dead_ in your repertoire, it becomes a signature spell in addition to your usual signature spells. If you're a prepared spellcaster with _animate dead_ in your spells known, spellbook, or the like, you can spend 10 minutes contemplating undeath to replace one of the spells you've prepared in your spell slots with an animate dead spell of the same level. In addition, if you're able to target the mostly intact remains of an appropriate type of dead creature when casting _animate dead_, the undead you animate gains a +1 status bonus to attack rolls, AC, saving throws, and skill checks for the duration of _animate dead_.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the reanimator archetype.

<title level="2">Reanimator Dedication leads to...</title>
[Bonds of Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=3489), [Deathly Secrets](/Feats.aspx?ID=3487), [Macabre Virtuoso](/Feats.aspx?ID=3488)

</title>

<traits>

</traits>

</column>

---

No means of creating or ruling the undead is beyond your grasp, even those of magical traditions not your own. You learn either the [_eyes of the dead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1104) or [_subjugate undead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1106) focus spell. If you don't already have one, you gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point, which you can Refocus by meditating over the earthly remains of a dead sentient creature. The rules for focus spells appear [here](/Rules.aspx?ID=276). Focus spells granted by the reanimator archetype are from the same tradition as those used to meet the archetype's prerequisite.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time, you learn a different spell and your focus pool increases by 1 Focus Point.

[Greater Deathly Secrets](/Feats.aspx?ID=3490), [Master of the Dead](/Feats.aspx?ID=3491)

<traits>

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 34

**Prerequisites**
[Reanimator Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3486); Expert in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), Expert in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or Expert in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)

</column>

---

Any necromancer can create [zombie](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=103) and [skeleton](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=92), but you know the secrets behind the creation of far more advanced undead monstrosities. You learn the [_create undead_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=10) rituals to create two types of common [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) for which you meet the prerequisites. (Your GM might give you access to additional types of undead.) You can't teach these rituals to anyone else and you can't participate in either ritual while allowing someone else to serve as the primary caster unless they also know the ritual. When you reach a new level, you can change either or both of these rituals to a different type of undead for which you now meet the prerequisites.

 When acting as primary caster, you can perform all _create undead_ rituals in 4 hours instead of 1 day and you gain a +2 circumstance bonus to your primary check. You can also perform the ritual without the aid of a secondary caster, in which case you attempt the secondary check.

**Special** You can select this feat more than once. Each time, you learn the rituals to create two more types of undead creatures.

<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 41

**Archetype** [Undead Master](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=176)

**Prerequisites**
evil alignment

</column>

---

You gain the services of an [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) companion that travels with you and obeys your commands. The rules for undead companions are under [Undead Companions](/Rules.aspx?ID=1690) and utilize those for [animal companions](/Rules.aspx?ID=149).

 Contrary to the usual rules for companions, as an undead master it's possible for you to have more than one undead companion at a time. However, only one of those companions, your “active companion,” follows you during exploration and encounters; the rest are reduced to an “inactive” state that can be easily tucked into an inventory or stored in a nearby crypt. If you ever have more than one undead companion, you gain the Call Companion action, with your undead companions taking the place of animal companions.

<document level="2" id="action-601" />

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the undead master archetype.

[Guardian Ghosts](/Feats.aspx?ID=3493), [Their Master's Call](/Feats.aspx?ID=3494)

once per 10 minutes

You would take damage from a Strike while one of your undead companions is adjacent to you.

You magically divert some of the harm from an incoming attack away from yourself, forcing your undead companion to take it in your stead. You can use [Treat Wounds](/Actions.aspx?ID=57) to restore Hit Points to [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) creatures, not just living ones. markdown:
<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Ghost Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3496) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 46

**Archetype** [Ghost](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=177)

**Prerequisites**
You died and returned as a ghost.

</column>

---

You have risen as a shell of your former self, a spirit of mist and anguish. You gain the [ghost](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=51), [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=149), and [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) traits, and the [basic undead benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=1694). Your undead craving is to settle your unfinished business. You also gain the [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) trait except you can't pass through solid objects unless you select the Pass Through feat. Being a ghost has the following major effects.

 **Floating** You can float but are still tethered to the ground. Replace your land Speed with an equal fly Speed. You can't rise more than a few inches above the ground when you [Fly](/Actions.aspx?ID=94). This means you can move above many types of difficult or hazardous terrain without moving slowly or being damaged, even though you can't fly without limit. You can [Leap](/Actions.aspx?ID=81), [High Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=36), [Long Jump](/Actions.aspx?ID=37), and take similar actions, and use your fly Speed for any calculations that would normally require your land Speed.

 **Items** You can transmute physical items to make them part of your incorporeal form. This requires spending 10 minutes with the items within reach, during which you transform the items into part of your form; you can return items you already have incorporated to a corporeal state at the same time. The items retain all their runes and other abilities, need to be invested normally if they have the [invested](/Traits.aspx?ID=98) trait, and need to be worn, held, or stowed appropriately. Once you've incorporated the items, you and other incorporeal creatures can use them normally—you can Interact with them, Release them, and so on. Your incorporated weapons gain the benefits of the [_ghost touch_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=297) property rune, allowing you to use them normally against both corporeal and incorporeal creatures. Incorporated items become corporeal again only if you transmute them back or are destroyed, in which case, they drop to the ground under you.

 **Attacks** Your unarmed attacks become [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103) and deal negative damage instead of their normal type.

 **Strength** Unlike most incorporeal creatures, your Strength modifier is not –5; you keep the same Strength score you had before you became a ghost, though you can only attempt Strength-based skill checks—typically [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) checks—against other incorporeal creatures, as normal for an incorporeal creature. Against incorporeal creatures, use your Strength normally to determine the results of Athletics checks, Strikes with melee weapons, and any other checks or damage rolls dependent on Strength.

 **Ties that Bind** When you become a ghost, work with your GM to choose a bound site and unfinished business, both of which matter for your character's story, as well as some ghost archetype feats. Your bound site tethers you to the physical world and is typically either a location important to you in life or the place where you died. Unfinished business keeps you from passing to the afterlife. If someone resolves your unfinished business, you decide whether to accept the change and pass on, or to fight it. If you pass on, you get a few minutes to say your goodbyes, and then move into the River of Souls and the afterlife. Your character ceases to be. If you fight the change, you remain, though you and the GM might determine a new unfinished business. If you are physically destroyed, you cease your existence as a ghost but still might not be able to pass on to the afterlife if your unfinished business is incomplete. In this liminal state, you might come across strange energies and become another sort of creature, or anchor to a [summoner](/Classes.aspx?ID=18) and become an eidolon. 

<title level="2">Ghost Dedication leads to...</title>
[Frightful Moan](/Feats.aspx?ID=3497), [Ghost Flight](/Feats.aspx?ID=3500), [Ghostly Grasp (Ghost)](/Feats.aspx?ID=3499), [Ghostly Resistance](/Feats.aspx?ID=3498), [Pass Through](/Feats.aspx?ID=3501), [Rejuvenation](/Feats.aspx?ID=3502)
name: Ghost Dedication
prerequisite: You died and returned as a ghost.

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 47 **Archetype** [Ghost](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=177) **Frequency** once per 10 minutes **Prerequisites** [Ghost Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3496); Master in [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) --- Filtering your form through the substance of an object, you can pass through walls, doors, and more. You Fly up to your Speed. During this movement, you can try to move through one object. Attempt an [Acrobatics](/Skills.aspx?ID=1) check as you try to enter its space. The DC is typically 30 to move through a wall of up to 5 feet, 15 for an ordinary door, and 10 for thinner structures like windows; the GM might set the DC higher for especially dense materials like [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=271) or lead, or for barriers that are magically reinforced. You can't Pass Through an obstacle made of magical force, such as a [_wall of force_](/Spells.aspx?ID=363). **Success** You move through the object, treating the square within it as difficult terrain. If you end your turn inside an object, you can move out of it only if you Pass Through again or use some other means of moving through a solid object. As normal for being [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222), starting your turn inside an object makes you [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35) for that turn.
**Failure** Your movement ends, and you trigger reactions as if you moved out of the square you started in.
name: Pass Through

>
[Ghoul Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3504) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 48

**Archetype** [Ghoul](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=178)

**Prerequisites**
You were killed by ghoul fever.

</column>

---

You have succumbed to ghoul fever, dying and returning as a [ghoul](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=52), an undead cursed with a never-ending hunger for dead flesh that slowly overrides your reason and willpower until you would do anything for the meal you crave. In addition to the personality changes, your body changes as well. Your ears become pointed, and your skin grows blueish and pale. Your fingernails sharpen into claws; your teeth become razor sharp, ready to tear flesh off the bone; and your tongue grows long and pointed.

 You gain the [ghoul](/Traits.aspx?ID=218) and [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) traits and the [basic undead benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=1694). Your undead craving is for the flesh of dead creatures; freshly dead corpses from sapient creatures fulfill your cravings much more than non-sapient or rotted corpses, but any dead creature can stave off the hunger for at least a little while. You gain two [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attacks in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) weapon group. The first unarmed attack is a claw that deals 1d4 slashing damage with the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170) and [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179) traits, and the second unarmed attack is a set of jaws that deal 1d6 piercing damage and have the finesse trait.

 You gain the Consume Flesh action. Satisfying your craving is difficult. Consuming Flesh temporarily satiates you. Many ghoul feats have extra abilities or functions that can be used when you are satiated, though using those abilities also causes you to lose your satiated status. You can always Consume Flesh, but eating more than a normal amount has no further effect; a ghoul's hunger is satiated, or it is not.

 **Consume Flesh** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)) **Requirements** You are adjacent to the corpse of a Small or larger creature that died in the last hour; **Effect** You devour a chunk of the corpse. You become satiated for 1 hour.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the ghoul archetype

<title level="2">Ghoul Dedication leads to...</title>
[Corpse Stench](/Feats.aspx?ID=3512), [Feverish Enzymes](/Feats.aspx?ID=3507), [Flailtongue](/Feats.aspx?ID=3888), [Glutton for Flesh](/Feats.aspx?ID=3511), [Grave Strength](/Feats.aspx?ID=3508), [Replenishing Consumption](/Feats.aspx?ID=3505), [Secret Eater](/Feats.aspx?ID=3890), [Sickening Bite](/Feats.aspx?ID=3510), [Swift Leap](/Feats.aspx?ID=3506), [Tunneling Claws](/Feats.aspx?ID=3891)
name: Ghoul Dedication
prerequisite: You were killed by ghoul fever.

Your enzymes can paralyze your foes rather than merely making it harder for them to heal their wounds. Strike with your claw or jaws. If you hit a living non-[elf](/Traits.aspx?ID=58) creature, it becomes [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28) unless it succeeds at a Fortitude save against your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. You have developed a capacity to store more flesh within your gaunt body to leave yourself satiated longer. If you [Consume Flesh](/Feats.aspx?ID=3504) while satiated, you become fully satiated. </title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 50

**Archetype** [Lich](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=179)

**Prerequisites**
Expert in [Crafting](/Skills.aspx?ID=4); living creature, ability to cast 6th-level or higher spells from spell slots, completed ritual to become a lich and crafted a _soul cage_

</column>

---

After years of study and careful planning, you finally completed a _soul cage_ to house your soul and successfully performed a ritual to transform yourself into a lich. Now, neither death nor time can prevent you from pursuing your studies and achieving your grand ambitions. You gain the undead trait and the [basic undead benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=1694). Your undead craving is for knowledge.

 You gain a unique [_soul cage_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1545)—a magic item that houses your soul. Whenever you would die, your soul flees to the _soul cage_ to allow you to be rebuilt. As long as your soul cage exists, you can't truly be destroyed.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the lich archetype.

<title level="2">Lich Dedication leads to...</title>
[Bolster Soul Cage](/Feats.aspx?ID=3517), [Drain Soul Cage](/Feats.aspx?ID=3514), [Enshroud Soul Cage](/Feats.aspx?ID=3515), [Hand of the Lich](/Feats.aspx?ID=3516), [Spell Gem](/Feats.aspx?ID=3518)

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 50

**Prerequisites**
[Lich Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3513); [Drain Bonded Item](/Actions.aspx?ID=13), spellbook

</column>

---

You make your [_soul cage_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1545) into your bonded item, allowing you to harness its abundant magical energy. Once per day, when you use Drain Bonded Item, you can choose any spell in your spellbook that you can cast, even if you haven't prepared or cast it that day. Your _soul cage_ doesn't need to be on your person for you to use Drain Bonded Item. If your _soul cage_ is broken or destroyed, you can't use Drain Soul Cage. Even if you can Drain Bonded Item more than once per day, for instance if you are a universalist wizard, you can still only choose a spell you haven't prepared and cast once per day.
name: Drain Soul Cage
prerequisite: Lich Dedication; Drain Bonded Item, spellbook

You wreathe your [_soul cage_](/Equipment.aspx?ID=1545) in an ever-growing collection of obfuscating illusions and protective abjurations to hide it from your enemies. You disguise the _soul cage_ as any non-magical object of the  same Bulk, and it gains the effects of the [_magic aura_](/Spells.aspx?ID=178) and [_nondetection_](/Spells.aspx?ID=209) spells. The effects have unlimited durations, are heightened to half your level rounded up, and use your spell DC against any attempt to [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) them. The magic aura makes your _soul cage_ appear non-magical. You can ignore the effects of any of these spells when dealing with your own _soul cage_. You are mentally alerted whenever your _soul cage_ is damaged.

</column>

---

Inspired by the degenerate [demiliches](/Monsters.aspx?ID=283) your kind sometimes devolves into, you've embedded a gem into your brow, fusing it to your necrotic flesh. This gem has been specially calibrated to hold one of the following spells: [_repulsion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=254), [_scrying_](/Spells.aspx?ID=268), or [_true seeing_](/Spells.aspx?ID=344). You must decide which spell your gem contains when you take this feat; changing the spell requires retraining the feat. Once per day, you can drain the gem's magical energy to Cast the Spell without spending a spell slot.

 At 18th level, you can heighten whichever spell you chose to 7th level. At 20th level, you can heighten whichever spell you chose to 8th level; regardless of which spell you chose, you can instead drain the gem's magical energy to cast an 8th-level [_spell turning_](/Spells.aspx?ID=297) without spending a spell slot.
name: Spell Gem

text: <title level="1" right="Feat 16" pfs="Standard" > Spell Gem Source Book of the Dead pg. 51 Archetype Lich Prerequisites Lich Dedication; Legendary in Crafting --- Inspired by the degenerate demiliches your kind sometimes devolves into, you've embedded a gem into your brow, fusing it to your necrotic flesh. This gem has been specially calibrated to hold one of the following spells: repulsion , scrying , or true seeing . You must decide which spell your gem contains when you take this feat; changing the spell requires retraining the feat. Once per day, you can drain the gem's magical energy to Cast the Spell without spending a spell slot. At 18th level, you can heighten whichever spell you chose to 7th level. At 20th level, you can heighten whichever spell you chose to 8th level; regardless of which spell you chose, you can instead drain the gem's magical energy to cast an 8th-level spell turning without spending a spell slot.

[Mummy Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3520) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 52

**Archetype** [Mummy](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=180)

**Prerequisites**
you are dead and were mummified (by natural or ritualistic means)

</column>

---

Whether through natural processes or foul rituals, your body was mummified, and you've risen as an undead mummy. You gain the [mummy](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=74) and [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) traits, as well as [basic undead benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=1694).

 Many effects that harm the living are far less effective against your desiccated form. Unfortunately, your dried-out body is also highly flammable. You gain the [Toughness](/Feats.aspx?ID=855) feat, but also [fire](/Traits.aspx?ID=72) weakness equal to half your level.

 Your fist draws moisture from the living by touch, making it more damaging and deadly. The damage die for your fist increases to 1d6 instead of 1d4, and your fist loses the [nonlethal](/Traits.aspx?ID=188) trait.

 Finally, you become supernaturally bound to the dominant terrain in which you were created, either because you formed naturally from the weather of that terrain or because of the local ingredients and methods used in an intentional mummification process. Choose arctic, desert, mountain, or swamp. This choice can't be changed and may alter the effects of some of your feats.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the mummy archetype.

<title level="2">Mummy Dedication leads to...</title>
[Accursed Touch](/Feats.aspx?ID=3525), [Desiccating Inhalation](/Feats.aspx?ID=3530), [Ensnaring Wrappings](/Feats.aspx?ID=3528), [Grave Mummification](/Feats.aspx?ID=3523), [Mummy's Despair](/Feats.aspx?ID=3524), [One with the Land](/Feats.aspx?ID=3521), [Semblance of Life](/Feats.aspx?ID=3522), [Storm Shroud](/Feats.aspx?ID=3526), [Terrain Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=3529)
name: Mummy Dedication

**Desert** Dust or sand
**Mountain** Clouds or mist
**Swamp** Rain or murky water

---

You've learned to harness the supernatural curse that animates you, imbuing your most powerful attacks with a terrible curse. When you critically hit with a fist Strike, negative energy binds to it; this is a [curse](/Traits.aspx?ID=38) and a [disease](/Traits.aspx?ID=46). The creature takes 2d6 [persistent negative damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29). While the creature has this persistent damage, it's also [stupefied 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37). The persistent damage increases to 3d6 at 14th level and 4d6 at 20th level. This is a [critical specialization effect](/Rules.aspx?ID=235).

<title level="2">Accursed Touch leads to...</title>
[Channel Rot](/Feats.aspx?ID=3527)
name: Accursed Touch

>
[Desiccating Inhalation](/Feats.aspx?ID=3530) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 53

**Archetype** [Mummy](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=180)

**Frequency**
once per hour

**Prerequisites**
[Mummy Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3520)

</column>

---

You draw in the moisture from nearby creatures, draining them dry to heal your wounds. Creatures in a 30-foot cone take 6d8 negative damage, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your class DC. A creature that critically fails this saving throw is also [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10). As long as at least one creature was damaged by your Desiccating Inhalation, you regain HP equal to your level.

 At 14th level and every 2 levels thereafter, the damage increases by 1d8.
name: Desiccating Inhalation

<title

    pfs="Standard"
>
[As in Life, So in Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=3532) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Skeleton" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=236" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 56

</column>

---

Specific memories of your old life are hard to hold onto, but you know things without remembering why. You gain the [Adopted Ancestry](/Feats.aspx?ID=751) feat. You can choose any ancestry, but it is likely to be one that matches both your skeleton heritage and who you were in life. As long as your body is completely covered by armor or clothing, you do not have to attempt [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) checks against a creature's Perception DC to successfully [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) yourself as a member of that ancestry. This is a non-magical disguise that doesn't protect against divination. This disguise doesn't provide any benefit against a creature actively attempting a Perception check against you.
name: As in Life, So in Death
