</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Skeleton" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=236" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 56

**Frequency**
once per 10 minutes

**Trigger**
An enemy's Strike against you is a critical hit.

</column>

---

You collapse into a pile of bones, mitigating the worst of the damage you would have taken, and the triggering attack deals only the amount it would deal on a hit (typically full damage instead of double damage). Any other effects caused by a critical hit still occur. While collapsed, you're [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) and can't act except to Stand, which re-forms you into a skeleton in a standing position.
name: Collapse

You lie [prone](/Conditions.aspx?ID=31) and pretend to be an ordinary skeleton. As long as you don't move or take any actions requiring anything other than your mind, you appear dead. This ability doesn't work against creatures that already know you're an animate undead unless you have changed your appearance.

<title

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Rejuvenation Token](/Feats.aspx?ID=3539) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Skeleton" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=236" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 56

</column>

---

You tie yourself to the [Material Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=1) by implanting a piece of your consciousness into a weapon, piece of armor, or other item that's precious to you. As long as this object is intact, even if your body is destroyed, you can be restored to the exact state you were in the last time you made daily preparations with this object in your possession. The soulbound object can be used as a special focus for [_raise dead_](/Spells.aspx?ID=243), [_resurrect_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=20), or similar magic. This warps the spell to bring you back in your skeletal undead state rather than bringing you back to life. [Pharasma](/Deities.aspx?ID=14) can't prevent you from returning when the spell is modified in this way.

 When you return, you permanently lose a memory that was precious to you, in addition to any other side effects of the spell that brought you back. Your soulbound object becomes inert until you spend 1 week of downtime to anchor yourself to it again, further fragmenting your mind.
name: Rejuvenation Token

  • You can't speak, Cast Spells, use [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104) actions requiring your hands, Activate magic items, or make any Strikes with your normal body.
  • You don't gain the [swarm mind](/MonsterAbilities.aspx?ID=36) ability, so you are still affected normally by [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) effects. You also retain the benefits of skeleton feats that don't require communication or the use of hands.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Vampire Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3545) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 58

**Archetype** [Vampire](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=181)

**Prerequisites**
You were a killed by a vampire drinking your blood.

</column>

---

You're a newly risen vampire. You gain the [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) and [vampire](/Traits.aspx?ID=242) traits and the [basic undead benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=1694), and your undead hunger is for the blood of the living. Your incisors elongate; you gain a fangs [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack that deals 1d6 piercing damage. They're in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group and have the [grapple](/Traits.aspx?ID=184) and [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) traits. You gain revulsion and sunlight vulnerabilities detailed in the Vampire Vulnerabilities sidebar and the Drink Blood ability.

 **Drink Blood** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48), [necromancy](/Traits.aspx?ID=117)) **Requirements** A [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20), [paralyzed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=28), [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33), [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38), or willing creature is within your reach; **Effect** You sink your fangs into that creature and drink its blood. This requires an [Athletics](/Skills.aspx?ID=3) check against the victim's Fortitude DC if the victim is grabbed, and automatically succeeds for any of the other conditions. If you succeed, the creature becomes [drained 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=10), and you gain temporary HP equal to the target's level that last for 10 minutes. Further uses against the target don't increase the drained condition or grant you more temporary HP.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the vampire archetype.

<title level="2">Vampire Dedication leads to...</title>
[Bat Form](/Feats.aspx?ID=3552), [Clinging Climber](/Feats.aspx?ID=3546), [Coffin Bound](/Feats.aspx?ID=3554), [Daywalker](/Feats.aspx?ID=3549), [Manipulative Charm](/Feats.aspx?ID=3547), [Nocturnal Kindred](/Feats.aspx?ID=3548), [Predatory Claws](/Feats.aspx?ID=3550), [Turn to Mist](/Feats.aspx?ID=3553), [Vicious Fangs](/Feats.aspx?ID=3551)

>
[Coffin Bound](/Feats.aspx?ID=3554) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Divine" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=48" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Negative" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=118" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 59

**Archetype** [Vampire](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=181)

**Prerequisites**
[Vampire Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3545)

</column>

---

You bind your spirit to a coffin filled with soil of your homeland, making it a place of recovery. If you rest inside your coffin for 10 minutes, you regain Hit Points equal to your Constitution modifier × half your level. You can still be healed in other ways during that time, though you're [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) and therefore unable to heal yourself. The GM might allow you to [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) while resting, depending on whether it's a type of Refocusing you can achieve while you slumber.

 If you would be destroyed, you instead remain near death. This doesn't change your [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=11) or [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=42) value, and you remain unconscious. After 1 hour, you're destroyed. If returned to your coffin before that hour is up, you avoid destruction; if you spend 1 hour resting in your coffin, you regain 1 HP and lose the dying and wounded conditions. You can't be healed in any other way when near death.

 Your coffin can't heal you if you're staked through the chest. You can be staked only if unconscious, and it takes three actions. You lose all benefits of this feat if your coffin is destroyed or the soil is lost. You must procure a new coffin and fill it with soil of your homeland to restore the feat's function.

<title level="2">Coffin Bound leads to...</title>
[Mist Escape](/Feats.aspx?ID=3555)
name: Coffin Bound

    right="Feat 14"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Mist Escape](/Feats.aspx?ID=3555) <actions string="Free Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 59

**Archetype** [Vampire](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=181)

**Prerequisites**
[Turn to Mist](/Feats.aspx?ID=3553); [Coffin Bound](/Feats.aspx?ID=3554)

**Trigger**
You are reduced to 0 HP.

</column>

---

As you fall, your body reacts to defend itself. You Turn to Mist. This doesn't expend a use of Turn to Mist, and you can use Mist Escape even if you've already Turned to Mist in the same day. You take [move](/Traits.aspx?ID=114) actions to move directly toward your coffin even though you are at 0 HP, though you aren't conscious and don't have control over how you do so. While at 0 HP in this form, you are unaffected by further damage. You automatically return to your corporeal form, [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38), if you reach your coffin or after 1 hour when you are destroyed, whichever one comes first.
name: Mist Escape

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />

**Prerequisites**

</column>

---

You stare into your target's eyes and enthrall them, shattering their free will. Once per day, you can cast 7th-level [_dominate_](/Spells.aspx?ID=87) as a divine innate spell, using your class DC or spell DC, whichever is higher. It gains the [visual](/Traits.aspx?ID=163) trait. At 18th level, the dominate is heightened to 8th level; at 20th level, it's heightened to 9th level. A creature that succeeds at its save is temporarily immune to your domination for 24 hours, though in most cases, you can't Cast the Spell again within 24 hours. If you are destroyed, all your _dominate_ spells from Dominating Gaze immediately end.
name: Dominating Gaze

<title

>
[Zombie Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3557) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 60

**Archetype** [Zombie](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=182)

**Prerequisites**
You died and were animated as a [husk zombie](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1919).

</column>

---

Despite your death and subsequent reanimation as a rotting corpse, you retain most of your mind and identity. Yet, it's always there: the hunger for the flesh and organs of the living. You gain the [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) and [zombie](/Traits.aspx?ID=245) traits, and the [basic undead benefits](/Rules.aspx?ID=1694). Unlike a typical zombie, you're not mindless. Reduce all your Speeds by 5 feet. Your fist loses the nonlethal trait.

 Because of its progressing state of decay, your body requires continual maintenance to remain at its best. Each day after your rest period, your body is deteriorated due to natural decay. Additionally, some zombie abilities allow you to push for a greater effect in exchange for a chance of deteriorating your body.

 While your body is deteriorated, you're [slowed 1](/Conditions.aspx?ID=35). You can spend 10 minutes checking and repairing your joints and other weak parts of your body to recover from deterioration. You can perform these repairs as part of your daily preparations. Because it's a natural result of your body's functions, you can't remove the slowed condition from deterioration through any other means.

 You crave the flesh of the living. You gain a jaws unarmed attack that deals 1d8 piercing damage. Your jaws are in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) group and have the [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) trait. You can use your jaws Strike only against a creature that's [grabbed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=20) or [restrained](/Conditions.aspx?ID=33) by you.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the zombie archetype.

<title level="2">Zombie Dedication leads to...</title>
[Ankle Biter](/Feats.aspx?ID=3558), [Feast](/Feats.aspx?ID=3559), [Festering Wound](/Feats.aspx?ID=3566), [Numb](/Feats.aspx?ID=3562), [Out of Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=3563), [Ravenous Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=3560), [Seize](/Feats.aspx?ID=3567), [Shamble](/Feats.aspx?ID=3564), [Unkillable](/Feats.aspx?ID=3565)
name: Zombie Dedication
prerequisite: You died and were animated as a husk zombie.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 8"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Out of Hand](/Feats.aspx?ID=3563) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Book of the Dead](/Sources.aspx?ID=118) pg. 61

**Archetype** [Zombie](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=182)

**Prerequisites**
[Zombie Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3557)

</column>

---

Even when your limbs are severed, they remain a part of you. When an arm is severed from your body, it gains the [minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=109) trait. While severed, your limb has the statistics of a [familiar](/Rules.aspx?ID=160) without any familiar or master abilities, except its Speed is 5 feet, it can't move further than 100 feet from you, it can Interact with things, and it can still make any [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) Strikes it could have made while attached to you (usually a fist Strike). Any Strikes it makes share your multiple attack penalty and use your attack bonus and damage. If your arm is reduced to 0 HP or is ever more than 100 feet from you, it becomes inert until reattached. The GM might allow you to detach other limbs that have unarmed attacks using the below action (for example, if you're a tiefling with [Form of the Fiend](/Feats.aspx?ID=1379), giving you a tail unarmed attack).

 You gain the Lay Down Arms action.

 **Lay Down Arms** <actions string="Single Action" /> You pull your arm off, harmlessly severing it from your body and dropping it in an adjacent square. You can also use this action to reattach your severed arm if it's adjacent to you; it immediately functions normally. If the detached limb was at 0 Hit Points, it takes 10 minutes to reattach it instead of a single action.
name: Out of Hand

---

Although you aren't a proper champion of your faith, your deity still recognizes your efforts and provides you with a small divine ability to help others. You gain the [_lay on hands_](/Spells.aspx?ID=395) devotion spell.

 You gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point or increase the number of Focus Points in your focus pool by 1. You refill your focus pool during your daily preparations, and you regain 1 Focus Point by spending 10 minutes using the [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) activity to pray to your deity or perform service toward their causes. The full rules for focus spells are [here](/Rules.aspx?ID=276). You are trained in divine spell attack rolls and spell DCs. Your spellcasting ability is Charisma.

 You must refrain from performing your deity's anathema or lose the ability to cast this spell until you atone.

Even when bloodshed is inevitable, you would rather see your foes surrender. You attempt a Diplomacy check to [Make an Impression](/Actions.aspx?ID=50) against a single foe whose Hit Points are at less than half of their maximum value, followed by an immediate [Request](/Actions.aspx?ID=51) to convince that creature to cease fighting. You take a –5 penalty to your Diplomacy check. The GM sets the DC of the Request based on the circumstances; it's generally at least a very hard DC for the creature's level. Some creatures might simply refuse, and those who agree to parley might find your arguments lacking and start fighting again.

---

A knight is nothing without their armor, and you know how to keep yours ready. You can perform a 10-minute ritual, which has the [conjuration](/Traits.aspx?ID=33) and [magical](/Traits.aspx?ID=103) traits, to divert a set of heavy armor you are wearing into an extradimensional space connected to you. While the armor is in this space, you can use a three-action activity, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), conjuration, and teleportation traits, to phase the armor back and instantly don it. The armor automatically phases away if you don another set of armor, if you become [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38), or if you die. If you are incapable of wearing the armor when it phases back, it appears in your square instead.
name: Instant Armor

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 75 **Archetype** [Knight Vigilant](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=27) **Prerequisites** [Knight Vigilant](/Feats.aspx?ID=1092); alignment permitted by the chosen deity --- Unwilling to be outdone by the Crimson Reclaimers and their oath, you've petitioned the gods of good for a sliver of divine magic. Choose one of the following deities whose requirements you meet—for the Any Deity option below, you can select from the following deities or a deity the GM deems appropriate: [Arazni](/Deities.aspx?ID=31), [Arqueros](/Deities.aspx?ID=244), [Falayna](/Deities.aspx?ID=119), [Gendowyn](/Deities.aspx?ID=152), [Iomedae](/Deities.aspx?ID=9), [Kazutal](/Deities.aspx?ID=41), [Kols](/Deities.aspx?ID=89), [Milani](/Deities.aspx?ID=43), [Pharasma](/Deities.aspx?ID=14), [Ragathiel](/Deities.aspx?ID=126), [Sarenrae](/Deities.aspx?ID=16), [Shelyn](/Deities.aspx?ID=17), [Suyuddha](/Deities.aspx?ID=245), [Vildeis](/Deities.aspx?ID=130)—and one of the listed spells. You can Cast that Spell once per day as a 4th-level divine innate spell, and you become trained in divine spell DCs and divine spell attack rolls. At 14th level, the spell heightens to 5th level; at 16th level, the spell heightens to 6th level. Once you've selected a deity and a spell, you can't change this selection. You don't need to worship the deity as your patron deity, as they are willing to grant this boon on behalf of your worthy cause. You must refrain from performing your deity's anathema or lose the ability to cast this spell until you atone.
  • **Any Deity**: [_freedom of movement_](/Spells.aspx?ID=128), [_remove curse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=250), [_resist energy_](/Spells.aspx?ID=256), [_spell immunity_](/Spells.aspx?ID=296), [_status_](/Spells.aspx?ID=308)
  • **Gendowyn**: [_barkskin_](/Spells.aspx?ID=20)
  • **Iomedae**: [_fire shield_](/Spells.aspx?ID=118)
  • [**Irori**](/Deities.aspx?ID=10): [_stoneskin_](/Spells.aspx?ID=312)
  • **Kazutal**: [_mage armor_](/Spells.aspx?ID=176), [_stoneskin_](/Spells.aspx?ID=312)
  • **Milani**: [_fire shield_](/Spells.aspx?ID=118), [_mage armor_](/Spells.aspx?ID=176)
  • **Ragathiel**: [_fire shield_](/Spells.aspx?ID=118)
  • **Sarenrae**: [_wall of fire_](/Spells.aspx?ID=362)
**Special** You can select this feat a second time at 14th level, gaining a second spell to cast once per day from your chosen deity's list or the Any Deity list, and you become an expert in divine spell DCs and divine spell attack rolls. You can select this feat a third time at 18th level. If you do, you gain a third spell to cast once per day from your chosen deity's list or the Any Deity list, and all three spells are heightened to 7th level.

You learn the [_for love, for lightning_](/Spells.aspx?ID=1108) focus spell. </title>

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Prerequisites**
[Knight Reclaimant Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1097); ability to cast divine spells

</column>

---

You call on the power of the Crimson Oath to gain magical aid. Choose one of the following spells: [_air walk_](/Spells.aspx?ID=6), [_dimensional anchor_](/Spells.aspx?ID=70), [_freedom of movement_](/Spells.aspx?ID=128), [_invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=164), [_remove curse_](/Spells.aspx?ID=250), [_searing light_](/Spells.aspx?ID=269). You can Cast that Spell once per day as a 4th-level divine innate spell. At 14th level, the spell heightens to 5th level, and at 16th level, the spell heightens to 6th level. If you anger the mysterious source of the Crimson Oath's power, you lose the ability to cast the spell until you atone.

**Special** You can select this feat a second time at 14th level, gaining a second spell from the list above, [_death ward_](/Spells.aspx?ID=64), or [_flame strike_](/Spells.aspx?ID=120), which you can cast once per day; you also become an expert in divine spell DCs and divine spell attack rolls. You can select this feat a third time at 18th level, gaining either a third spell from the list above, _death ward_, _flame strike_, or [_sunburst_](/Spells.aspx?ID=326), which you can cast once per day; additionally, all three spells from this feat heighten to 7th level, and you become a master of divine spell attacks and spell DCs.

[Lastwall Sentry Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=882); [Grave Sense](/Feats.aspx?ID=885)

</column>

---

Your ability to sense undead has improved. You sense undead as an [imprecise](/Rules.aspx?ID=412) sense with a range of 60 feet: an uncomfortable sensation brushes against your spirit and stinks of rot. When in proximity to an undead, you can sense its presence, but it has the [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) condition instead of the [observed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=27) condition. An undead using a disguise or otherwise trying to hide its presence must attempt a [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) or [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15) check against your Perception DC to hide its presence from you. If the creature succeeds, it's [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39), and you have to use the [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) basic action to detect the creature. As with hearing and other imprecise senses, you still need to Seek to locate an undetected creature.
name: Grave Sight

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 80

**Archetype** [Assassin](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=48)

**Prerequisites**
[Assassin Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=1890)

**Access**
Knights of Lastwall have access to this feat.

**Requirements**
Your mark is an [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) creature.

</column>

---

To aid with your mission of destroying undead, you've specialized in techniques to destroy them, much as other assassins learn to kill the living. When you Strike a [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) undead foe with a weapon that has the [backstabber](/Traits.aspx?ID=172) weapon trait, you deal 3 extra precision damage instead of 1. If the weapon is a +3 weapon, you deal 6 extra precision damage instead of 2. If you have the [Angel of Death](/Feats.aspx?ID=1893) feat, your attacks also instantly destroy undead at 0 Hit Points, and attempts for the undead to rejuvenate—such as via a [lich's](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=68) _soul cage_ or a [ghost's](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=51) rejuvenation ability—fail unless the effect's [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) level is higher than half your level when you killed the creature (rounded up), or originates from an [artifact](/Traits.aspx?ID=253) or deity. Finally, if you have the [Assassinate](/Feats.aspx?ID=1894) feat and an undead mark critically fails its save against your Assassinate, it is destroyed.
name: Angel of Vindication
requirement: Your mark is an  undead  creature.
requirement_markdown: Your mark is an [undead](/Traits.aspx?ID=160) creature.

You provide preventative remedies and care to help your patient fight off future maladies. You Treat a Condition the target doesn't yet have, naming any condition you could normally treat with Treat Condition. The [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check gains the [secret](/Traits.aspx?ID=142) trait, so the GM rolls it secretly. The next time within the next minute the creature would be affected by that condition, your treatment immediately attempts to reduce the condition value with the effects of Treat Condition, using the secret roll result for the check. Preventative Treatment lasts on a creature for 1 minute, until the treatment is used, or until you use Preventative Treatment again on that creature, whichever comes first.

You are one of the raiders eagerly planning to launch an assault by sea on the Whispering Tyrant's Isle of Terror. You gain the [Sudden Charge](/Feats.aspx?ID=134) fighter feat, though it's a viking feat for you instead. As normal when gaining an additional feat from an archetype feat, gaining Sudden Charge doesn't count toward fulfilling the special requirement for Viking Dedication. If you already had Sudden Charge, you can retrain it as part of gaining this feat. When you use Sudden Charge to Strike a target in shallow water, the target is [flat-footed](/Conditions.aspx?ID=16) against your Strike, as you use the water kicked up by your passage to camouflage your angle of attack. If you have [Viking Weapon Familiarity](/Feats.aspx?ID=2096) or [Viking Weapon Specialist](/Feats.aspx?ID=2097), add the [bastard sword](/Weapons.aspx?ID=15) and [rapier](/Weapons.aspx?ID=36) to the list of weapons in those feats.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Sorcerer" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=148" />
<trait label="Witch" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=323" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Knights of Lastwall](/Sources.aspx?ID=123) pg. 83

**Prerequisites**
a [familiar](Familiars.aspx), you follow a good-aligned deity or patron

**Access**
Knights of Lastwall have access to this feat.

</column>

---

Your familiar is a divine emissary, sent to you by your deity or patron and infused with celestial powers. You can select one additional familiar ability each day, which must be one of the following divine emissary familiar abilities. You can't select more than one divine emissary familiar ability at a time.

 **Erudite** Your familiar has incredible religious knowledge. Despite being a minion, your familiar gains 1 reaction at the start of its turns, which it can use only to [Aid](/Actions.aspx?ID=75) you on a [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13) check (it still has to prepare to help you as normal for the Aid reaction). It automatically succeeds its check to Aid you with Religion checks or automatically critically succeeds if you're a master in Religion.

 **Luminous** Your familiar glows with a comforting light. It sheds bright light in a 30-foot radius and dim light for the next 30 feet. It can suppress or resume this light by using an action, which has the [concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32) trait.

 **Medic** Your familiar can draw upon the power of your deity to Cast a Spell once per day. The familiar can cast the 1-action version of [_heal_](/Spells.aspx?ID=148) at a level 2 levels lower than your highest-level spell slot, which it can cast only on you. You must be able to cast 3rd-level spells from spell slots to select this ability.

 **Radiant** Your familiar is filled with a divine radiance that makes it resistant to the forces of evil. Your familiar gains resistance to evil and [negative](/Traits.aspx?ID=118) damage equal to half your level.

**Trigger**

</column>

---

You use your shield in tandem with an ally's, forming a barricade. Both you and the triggering creature have [standard cover](/Rules.aspx?ID=459) as long as you remain adjacent to each other and you both have your shields raised; when this is no longer the case, the effect ends. You and your ally can't use this cover to [Hide](/Actions.aspx?ID=62), as it's obvious you're standing there holding your shields, but you and your ally can use it to [Take Cover](/Actions.aspx?ID=90). Normally, if you and your ally don't move, Shield Wall lasts until the beginning of your next turn, when your shield is no longer raised.

</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Outlaws of Alkenstar</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Abjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=2" />
<trait label="Aftermath" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=424" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Pathfinder #180: The Smoking Gun](/Sources.aspx?ID=125) pg. 77

**Prerequisites**
You were present at the death of the [medusa](/Monsters.aspx?ID=297) Alethsia, whose vitrumantic powers were passed on to you in the wake of her destruction.

</column>

---

Even if vitrumancy is a mystery to you, your blood and flesh know the secrets of the art of arcane glass. Patches of your skin to flicker into glass without warning. By focusing the effect, you can concentrate the glass into a powerful protective layer of magical obsidian. Once per day, you can cast [_stoneskin_](/Spells.aspx?ID=312) on yourself as an innate primal spell, though the spell covers you in a layer of glass instead of stone. During this innate stoneskin, you gain the Shatter Glass reaction. At 18th level, the stoneskin is heightened to 6th level instead of 4th.

**Shatter Glass**<actions string="Reaction" /> **Trigger** An adjacent creature Strikes you with a melee weapon or [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack and deals damage; **Requirements** Your innate _stoneskin_ from Glass Skin is active; **Effect** You shatter some of the glass on your skin to damage your attacker. The attacker takes 3d10 damage and the duration of the _stoneskin_ decreases by 1 minute. At 14th level, the damage increases to 4d10, and at 18th level, the damage increases to 5d10.

<traits>

---

You built your reanimated construct companion of modular components from various corpses. Its unique makeup enables your companion to split into dozens or even hundreds of much smaller corpse constructs. Acting as one, this shambling swarm can overwhelm your enemies. 

You Command your reanimated construct companion. Instead of its normal actions, the companion splits into a horde of Small and Tiny construct companions within a 30-foot emanation from its original space. The horde makes a Strike against each foe within the emanation with a +2 circumstance bonus to its attack rolls. The multiple attack penalty doesn't increase until after the companion makes all the attacks. The miniature companions recombine into a single companion of their original size at any location within the emanation.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Amp" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=425" />
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />

<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Psychic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=430" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 27

</column>

---

Your spell reaches into the mind of a creature and removes you from it. The amped cantrip must be one that has one or more targets and must either require a spell attack roll or have a saving throw. Use this amp in place of the psi cantrip's normal amp entry.

---
**Amp** Choose one target of the spell or one creature in its area. If that enemy fails its save or the spell hits it, you become [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) by that creature, disappearing from its senses for 1 minute or until you use a [hostile action](/Rules.aspx?ID=300). This is similar to being [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26), but effects like [_see invisibility_](/Spells.aspx?ID=271) don't reveal you—you're affecting the target's mind, not its vision. [_True seeing_](/Spells.aspx?ID=344) can still see through this illusion if the [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check succeeds.
name: Remove Presence

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Divination" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=47" />
<trait label="Mental" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=106" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />
<trait label="Psychic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=430" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 27

</column>

---

You can detect the flickers of mental activity let off by all thinking creatures. You gain thoughtsense as a [vague](/Rules.aspx?ID=413) sense that has a range of 30 feet—like all vague senses, it's only about as precise as an average human's sense of smell, meaning you generally can predict only if a creature is present. Your thoughtsense detects only thinking creatures, so a creature that is unthinking or otherwise immune to mental effects (such as many constructs and oozes) can't be perceived using your thoughtsense, regardless of how precise it is. 

While your [Psyche is Unleashed](/Actions.aspx?ID=1222), your thoughtsense upgrades to an imprecise [sense](/Rules.aspx?ID=412), letting you use it to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) out creatures.
name: Thoughtsense

<traits>

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 27

</column>

---

Your spell leaves a lingering connection between you and a creature—one through which you can nudge the creature's mind this way or that. The amped cantrip must take 2 or more actions to cast, target one or more creatures, and either require a spell attack roll or have a saving throw. Use this amp in place of the psi cantrip's normal amp entry.

---
**Amp** Choose one enemy who is a target of the spell. If that enemy fails its save or the spell hits it, you whisper in the creature's mind, forcing it to Step in a direction of your choosing; as this is [forced movement](/Rules.aspx?ID=451), you can't force the creature to Step into hazardous terrain, off a ledge, or the like. After it Steps, the creature becomes temporarily immune to this amp for 24 hours.
name: Whispering Steps

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Illusion" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=92" />
<trait label="Occult" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=120" />

**Prerequisites**
[wandering reverie](/SubconsciousMinds.aspx?ID=4) subconscious mind

</column>

---

You Stride into a willing ally's space, at which point both of your appearances shift into a shared third appearance, usually one that looks like a mix of the two of you. Then, either you or your ally Steps. You each maintain the merged appearance. Creatures who are observing this know what happened, but still must [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) or otherwise engage with the illusion to attempt to disbelieve it and determine which of you is which. Otherwise, they can't tell the difference and have an equal chance to target each of you (DC 11 flat check). This illusion ends as soon as either you or the ally you're merged with acts.
name: Dream Guise

**Trigger**
A non-[minion](/Traits.aspx?ID=109) ally within 60 feet is reduced to 0 Hit Points.

</column>

---

The shock of seeing your ally near death breaks whatever limits exist in your mind, sending your power spilling forth. If your psyche is currently unleashed, you can immediately use a [psyche](/Traits.aspx?ID=429) action that takes 1 action or less to use. If your psyche is not currently unleashed, you [Unleash your Psyche](/Actions.aspx?ID=1222), which remains unleashed until the end of your next turn. You can ignore Unleash Psyche's requirement of needing to have Cast a Spell on your previous turn, but you still can't Unleash your Psyche if you're [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) or for 2 rounds after your psyche subsides.

---

The sheer power of your magic fractures reality. Use this amp in place of a psi cantrip's normal amp entry. The cantrip must be one that takes 2 or more actions to cast.

---
**Amp** You or one target of the spell are surrounded by a spiral of torn space. This is an aura, and you choose the radius of the emanation, up to 20 feet. A creature that starts its turn in the aura or enters the aura during its turn takes 1d6 slashing damage for every level of the amped psi cantrip, with a [basic](/Rules.aspx?ID=329) Reflex save against your spell DC. If the creature critically fails, the torn space throws it off balance and it falls prone. The aura lasts until the beginning of your next turn. You can choose whether the aura affects the creature emitting it.
name: Shatter Space

[Diverse Lore](/Feats.aspx?ID=3699) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

</column>

---

Your wandering studies mean you've heard rumors or theories about almost every topic... though admittedly, your sources aren't always the most reliable. You can take a –2 penalty to your check to [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) with [Esoteric Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) to Recall Knowledge about any topic, not just the usual topics available for Esoteric Lore. Additionally, when you succeed at your check to [Exploit a Vulnerability](/Actions.aspx?ID=1227), compare the result of your Esoteric Lore check to the DC to Recall Knowledge for that creature; if that number would be a success or a critical success, you gain information as if you had succeeded at the Recall Knowledge check.
name: Diverse Lore

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Root to Life](/Feats.aspx?ID=3702) <actions string="Single Action or Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Esoterica" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=427" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Necromancy" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=117" />
<trait label="Primal" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=134" />
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 42

</column>

---

Marigold, spider lily, pennyroyal—many primal traditions connect flowers and plants with the boundary between life and death, and you can leverage this association to keep an ally on this side of the line. You place a small plant or similar symbol on an adjacent [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=11) creature, immediately stabilizing them; the creature is no longer dying and is instead [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) at 0 Hit Points.

 If you spend 2 actions instead of 1, you empower the act further by uttering a quick folk blessing to chase away ongoing pain, adding the [auditory](/Traits.aspx?ID=16) trait to the action. When you do so, attempt flat checks to remove each source of [persistent damage](/Conditions.aspx?ID=29) affecting the target; due to the particularly effective assistance, the DC is 10 instead of the usual 15.
name: Root to Life

Your multidisciplinary study of magic means you know how to activate the magic in [scrolls](/Equipment.aspx?Category=15&Subcategory=52) with ease. You can activate scrolls of any magical tradition, using your thaumaturge class DC for the scroll's DC, rather than a particular spell DC. If a spell is on the spell list for multiple traditions, you choose which tradition to use at the time you activate the scroll. You can draw and activate scrolls with the same hand holding an implement, much like you can for esoterica.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Call Implement](/Feats.aspx?ID=3704) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Teleportation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=156" />
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 42

**Requirements**
You have a free hand.

</column>

---

You can tug on the bonds of ownership between yourself and your [implement](Implements.aspx), causing it to find its way back to you. You look down and find that your implement has mysteriously appeared in your free hand, as long as the implement was within 1 mile and on the same plane of existence. If your implement is attended by another creature, that creature can prevent the implement from teleporting away if it succeeds at a Will save against your class DC. If the creature succeeds, you can't attempt to Call that Implement again; you must track the creature down to get the implement back.
name: Call Implement
requirement: You have a free hand.

[Talisman Esoterica](/Feats.aspx?ID=3706) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Esoterica" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=427" />
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 43

</column>

---

You know how to assemble the supernatural objects in your esoterica into a number of temporary [talismans](/Equipment.aspx?Category=15&Subcategory=19). Each day during your daily preparations, you can make two talismans with an item level no higher than half your level. You must know each talisman's formula. A talisman created this way is a temporary item and loses its magic the next time you make your daily preparations.

You know the formulas for all common talismans in the _Core Rulebook_ of your level or lower. You remember your talisman formulas through oral tradition or mnemonics, so you don't need a [formula book](/Equipment.aspx?ID=22) for them.

<title level="2">Talisman Esoterica leads to...</title>
[Elaborate Talisman Esoterica](/Feats.aspx?ID=3716), [Grand Talisman Esoterica](/Feats.aspx?ID=3725)

<traits>

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 43

**Prerequisites**
[Exploit Vulnerability](/Actions.aspx?ID=1227)

---

You can find the one weak point in a creature's scales, wards, or armor to get past its resistances. When you succeed at Exploit Vulnerability, you learn about the highest of the creature's resistances that can be bypassed (for example, if the creature has resistance to physical damage except silver), if the creature has one. If you prefer, you can choose the following benefit instead of one of the usual two benefits from Exploit Vulnerability.

 **Breached Defenses** You can choose this benefit only if you succeeded at Exploit Vulnerability and learned the creature has at least one resistance that can be bypassed. Choose one such resistance. Your unarmed and weapon Strikes bypass the chosen resistance.

</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 44

</column>

---

You break a trinket such as a lodestone or jade pendant in two, creating a sympathetic link between the halves that bridges distance. During your daily preparations, you perform a short ceremony where you gift one of the two halves to a willing ally. On that ally, you can cast spells and use thaumaturge abilities that have a range of touch at a range of 30 feet instead, and the ally can cast spells that have a range of touch on you from a range of 30 feet. These effects last as long as you and the ally have their half; if either half leaves either of your possession for even a moment, or if you establish a link with a new ally during your next daily preparations, the link breaks.

<title
    level="1"

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Sympathetic Vulnerabilities](/Feats.aspx?ID=3714) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 45

**Prerequisites**
[Exploit Vulnerability](/Actions.aspx?ID=1227), mortal weakness or personal antithesis

</column>

---

When you apply your will to invoke a vulnerability, the result is more powerful, and the vulnerability ripples out in a web from your main target to affect a broader range of creatures. This has one of two effects, based on the type of vulnerability you invoked.

 While you have mortal weakness applied, your Strikes also apply that weakness against any creature that has that weakness, not just creatures of the exact same kind. For instance, if you used mortal weakness against a [red dragon](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=168) to apply its weakness to cold to your Strikes, those Strikes would also apply to the weakness to cold of [fire elementals](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=43) or any other creature with a weakness to cold.

 While you have personal antithesis applied to a non-[humanoid](/Traits.aspx?ID=91) creature, you can apply your custom weakness to all creatures of the exact same kind. For example, if you used personal antithesis against an [imp](/Monsters.aspx?ID=109), the custom weakness would apply to other imps but not to other non-imp [devils](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=30).
name: Sympathetic Vulnerabilities

    pfs="Standard"
>
[Twin Weakness](/Feats.aspx?ID=3719) <actions string="Two Actions" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Esoterica" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=427" />
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 45

**Prerequisites**
mortal weakness or personal antithesis

**Requirements**
You're holding an [implement](Implements.aspx) and a weapon, you are using [Exploit Vulnerability](/Actions.aspx?ID=1227) with mortal weakness or personal antithesis, and the target creature is within reach of both your implement and weapon.

</column>

---

As you make an attack augmented by your esoterica, you also press your implement against the creature, applying its weakness as your implement's energies sear the creature's flesh. Make a melee Strike against the target of your Exploit Vulnerability. On any attack roll result but a critical failure, you also press your implement against the creature, automatically dealing the additional damage from Exploit Vulnerability. This is in addition to any damage from your Strike, including the weakness the Strike applies from Exploit Vulnerability. This counts as two attacks when calculating your multiple attack penalty.

---

You have claimed an area or location as your demesne, granting you the ability to ward and protect it. When you select this feat, choose a demesne, an area of no more than 2,000 square feet. You must legitimately own the area or, if its a public area, you must lay claim to the area without anyone contesting it.

 Once you've chosen your demesne, it's automatically protected by an arcane [_private sanctum_](/Spells.aspx?ID=235) spell with an unlimited duration, heightened to half your level rounded up and using your thaumaturge class DC in place of a spell DC, if necessary. Additionally, the demesne is attended by three unseen custodians, as a successful [_unseen custodians_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=39) ritual, and one object in the area gains an elemental sentinel, as a successful [_elemental sentinel_](/Rituals.aspx?ID=57) ritual.

[Unlimited Demesne](/Feats.aspx?ID=3734)

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Evocation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=65" />
<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 47

**Requirements**
You're holding an [implement](Implements.aspx).

</column>

---

Your implement supercharges your weapon to shoot an impossible volley or carve through your foes. Make a Strike with your weapon against each enemy within 30 feet of you. You don't increase your multiple attack penalty until after making all the attacks. If your weapon is a melee weapon and any of the attacks are outside your reach, you Release the weapon before the Strikes, and it returns to your grasp after all of them. If your hands are full when the weapon returns, it falls to the ground in your space.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 47

**Prerequisites**
[Share Weakness](/Feats.aspx?ID=3717)

</column>

---

You've nurtured your bonds with your comrades, allowing you to share the benefits of your esoterica. When you use [Exploit Vulnerability](/Actions.aspx?ID=1227) and choose mortal weakness, select any number of allies within 30 feet of you. Their Strikes apply the weakness from mortal weakness the same way your Strikes do. This benefit ends when you stop benefiting from Exploit Vulnerability. Since this effect depends on magically strengthening your bond to your allies, only allies with whom you've developed a rapport over the course of one or more days gain the benefit.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Arcane" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=11" />
<trait label="Conjuration" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=33" />
<trait label="Thaumaturge" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=432" />
</traits>

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 47

**Prerequisites**
[Thaumaturge's Demesne](/Feats.aspx?ID=3723)

</column>

---

You can move your demesne here and there, bringing it wherever your journey takes you. Your demesne expands to a maximum of 10,000 square feet. Once per day, you can call your demesne forth, which takes 1 minute. This has the effects of [_resplendent mansion_](/Spells.aspx?ID=257), except that it conjures your demesne from its previous location, with all the benefits of Thaumaturge's Demesne in addition to the those of the spell. You must be able to claim the new area, with the same restrictions as Thaumaturge's Demesne.
name: Unlimited Demesne

[Wonder Worker](/Feats.aspx?ID=3735) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 47

**Prerequisites**
Legendary in [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), Legendary in [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), Legendary in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or Legendary in [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13)

</column>

---

The thaumaturge's path culminates with the working of wonders. Once per day, you can align your esoterica to cast a spell of 8th level or lower that takes 1, 2, or 3 actions to cast. The spell must be common or one to which you have access. You can choose a spell of any tradition for which you're legendary in the associated skill (Arcana for [arcane](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=1), Nature for [primal](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=4), Occultism for [occult](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=3), or Religion for [divine](/SpellLists.aspx?Tradition=2)). Use your thaumaturge class DC in place of any necessary spell DC and your thaumaturge class DC – 10 in place of any necessary [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) modifier or spell attack modifier.

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 2"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Psychic Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3736) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
<trait label="Multiclass" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=115" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 48

**Archetype** [Psychic](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=185)

**Prerequisites**
Intelligence 14 or Charisma 14

</column>

---

You feel something awaken within your mind. You become trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11); if you were already trained in Occultism, you become trained in a skill of your choice. You cast spells like a [psychic](/Classes.aspx?ID=21) and gain the Cast a Spell activity; as you don't have a subconscious mind, your thought components are simple intentions. Choose a [conscious mind](ConsciousMinds.aspx). You gain a spell repertoire with one standard psi cantrip of your choice from your conscious mind, which you cast as a psi cantrip. You gain the normal benefits and the amp for this psi cantrip, but not any other benefits from the conscious mind. If you don't have one, you gain a focus pool of 1 Focus Point, which you can use to amp your psi cantrips, and you can [Refocus](/Actions.aspx?ID=71) by meditating on your new powers. If you already have a focus pool, increase the number of points in your pool by 1. You're trained in occult spell attack rolls and occult spell DCs. Your key spellcasting ability for psychic archetype spells is the ability you used to qualify for the archetype, and they are occult psychic spells.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you have gained two other feats from the psychic archetype.

<title level="2">Psychic Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Psychic Spellcasting](/Feats.aspx?ID=3738), [Basic Thoughtform](/Feats.aspx?ID=3737), [Psi Development](/Feats.aspx?ID=3740)
name: Psychic Dedication

[Thaumaturge Dedication](/Feats.aspx?ID=3743) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
<trait label="Multiclass" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=115" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 49

**Archetype** [Thaumaturge](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=186)

**Prerequisites**
Charisma 14

</column>

---

You've uncovered basic thaumaturgy. You become trained in thaumaturge class DC. Choose an [implement](Implements.aspx); you can use it to Glimpse Vulnerability, but don't gain its benefits. You also gain a few esoterica, allowing you to use [esoterica](/Traits.aspx?ID=427) actions. You become trained in your choice of [Arcana](/Skills.aspx?ID=2), [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10), [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11), or [Religion](/Skills.aspx?ID=13); if you were already trained in these, you become trained in a skill of your choice. You gain the Glimpse Vulnerability action.

 **Glimpse Vulnerability** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([esoterica](/Traits.aspx?ID=427), [manipulate](/Traits.aspx?ID=104)); **Frequency** once per round; **Requirement** You are holding your implement; **Effect** You glimpse a hidden vulnerability and then strengthen it to aid you. Select a creature you can see. Until you Glimpse Vulnerability again, that target gains weakness 2 against your [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) and weapon Strikes.

<title level="2">Thaumaturge Dedication leads to...</title>
[Basic Thaumaturgy](/Feats.aspx?ID=3744), [Implement Initiate](/Feats.aspx?ID=3746), [Magical Knowledge](/Feats.aspx?ID=3747), [Resolute](/Feats.aspx?ID=3748)

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Devil's Eye](/Feats.aspx?ID=3749) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Aftermath" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=424" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 55

**Prerequisites**
You made a bargain with a [devil](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=30) or won a legal case or other similar duel of wits against a devil.

</column>

---

Your experience in the finer points of bargaining with a devil has awakened a sinister power that now inhabits your left eye. The eye is the same shape and iris color as your normal eye would be, but the sclera is a deep red instead of white and the pupil is a narrow, vertical slit. The eye grants you an abnormal understanding of the loopholes and legal processes employed to trap poor creatures that don't know any better. You gain the Objection reaction. You also become an expert in [Legal Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) and gain a +1 circumstance bonus to any check you make to read or negotiate a treatise, contract, or similar text. At 7th level you become a master of Legal Lore, and at 15th level you become legendary in Legal Lore. You can use Legal Lore in place of Perception to detect verbal loopholes, double entendres, hidden meanings, code, or contradictions in a conversation you can hear. This doesn't let you fully understand coded speech but alerts you to its presence.

 **Objection** <actions string="Reaction" /> ([fortune](/Traits.aspx?ID=76)) **Frequency** once per minute; **Trigger** You're about to attempt a saving throw against a [linguistic](/Traits.aspx?ID=101) effect; **Effect** Your devil's eye crackles with infernal glee as you discover a loophole in the wording of the triggering effect. You roll your saving throw twice, taking the higher result.
name: Devil's Eye

<title
    level="1"
    right="Feat 4"
    pfs="Limited"
>
[Echo of the Fallen](/Feats.aspx?ID=3750) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Aftermath" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=424" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 55

**Prerequisites**
You helped to lay a [haunt](/Traits.aspx?ID=88), [ghost](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=51), or [spirit](/Traits.aspx?ID=149) to rest.

</column>

---

With the utmost gratitude for your help in releasing them from their unearthly coil, a tiny sliver of a ghostly entity has remained attached to you. This manifests as an echo of their former self that follows you around and that you and anyone capable of casting [divine](/Traits.aspx?ID=48) or [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120) spells can see and speak with. When you take this feat, work with your GM to choose one martial weapon and one skill (or an advanced weapon if you're trained in all martial weapons) that are appropriate for the spirit; once you've chosen the weapon and skill, you can't change them. You gain the Accept Echo action.

 **Accept Echo** <actions string="Single Action" /> ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Frequency** once per day; **Effect** You allow the echo to inhabit your body, gaining a glowing aura around you, shining pale-green irises, a resonating voice, and the silhouette of the spirit around your own body, all of which can be seen clearly by others. While in this state, you become trained in the weapon you chose and an expert in the skill you chose. Additionally, while you're in this state, the echo can speak and interact with the [Material Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=1) using your body, and you gain a +4 status bonus to all saves against possession effects, as the possessing spirit protects you from other possessions.

 This state lasts for 10 minutes, after which the echo disappears completely until the next time you make your daily preparations. You can Dismiss this effect.

 At 7th level you become a master of the skill you chose, at 13th level you become an expert with the weapon you chose, and at 15th level you become legendary with the skill you chose.
name: Echo of the Fallen
prerequisite: You helped to lay a haunt, ghost, or spirit to rest.

[Lingering Chill](/Feats.aspx?ID=3751) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Aftermath" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=424" />
<trait label="Cold" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=27" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 55

**Prerequisites**
You've been brought to 0 Hit Points by an enemy that has the [cold](/Traits.aspx?ID=27) trait or an enemy's ability that has the cold trait.

</column>

---

The chill of ice entered your veins and never left, adjusting the internal temperature of your body. Your breath comes out in puffs, and your skin is as cold and smooth as the ice in your veins. You can cast [_ray of frost_](/Spells.aspx?ID=245) as a primal innate cantrip. You gain resistance to cold damage equal to half your level, and you're protected from [severe cold temperatures](/Rules.aspx?ID=642).

>
[Petrified Skin](/Feats.aspx?ID=3756) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Aftermath" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=424" />
<trait label="Transmutation" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=157" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 56

**Prerequisites**
You have been [petrified](/Conditions.aspx?ID=30) by an enemy.

</column>

---

It might have been a [medusa](/Monsters.aspx?ID=297), [dracolisk](/Monsters.aspx?ID=565), or even a [fossil golem](/Monsters.aspx?ID=1174); regardless of the source, you were the target of some petrifying effect, and an element of that stony gaze has remained with you, both protecting and slowly consuming you. Your limbs are coated with a layer of stone that rests atop your skin and covers more of your body as you lose health. You gain a stone fist [unarmed](/Traits.aspx?ID=199) attack that deals 1d8 bludgeoning damage, has the [shove](/Actions.aspx?ID=38) trait, and is in the [brawling](/WeaponGroups.aspx?ID=4) weapon group (unlike a normal fist, it doesn't have the [agile](/Traits.aspx?ID=170) or [finesse](/Traits.aspx?ID=179) traits).

 Additionally, you become more petrified as your life force ebbs. When you have fewer than half your maximum Hit Points, you increase the damage die size of your stone fist from 1d8 to 1d10 and gain resistance to physical damage (except [adamantine](/Equipment.aspx?ID=374)) equal to your Constitution modifier.

 If you would gain the [dying](/Conditions.aspx?ID=11) condition, you can choose to instead be permanently petrified and avoid the risk of death. When you do, you enter your petrified form with your full maximum Hit Points instead of the normal number. If you become unpetrified, you return to 0 Hit Points, as normal. You can't voluntarily end this petrification. [Counteracting](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) this petrification requires a casting of [_stone to flesh_](/Spells.aspx?ID=311) of a spell level equal to at least half your level, and a successful counteract check against the hard DC for your level. Other effects like _stone to flesh_ have similar limitations, as determined by the GM. Each time you recover from this petrification, you gain a new scar on your skin in the shape of a long, thin crack.
name: Petrified Skin
prerequisite: You have been petrified by an enemy.
prerequisite_markdown: You have been [petrified](/Conditions.aspx?ID=30) by an enemy.

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 57

**Prerequisites**
You helped to save a [fey](/Traits.aspx?ID=69) from a terrible fate, and you're not a fey.

</column>

---

There are some fates worse than death–and you worked to save a fey from one such fate. In return, your life became bound to theirs. Fey magic has since become a part of you, bringing the vibrant colors of the [First World](/Planes.aspx?ID=10) to you and all that surrounds you. Your skin, hair, all that you touch, and anything within 5 feet of you changes to the most brilliant hues possible, though the colors fade as you cease to touch an object or you move away. You gain the ability to cast [_summon fey_](/Spells.aspx?ID=322) as a 7th-level primal innate spell once per day. At 18th level the spell heightens to 8th level, and at 20th level it heightens to 9th level.

 The first time you die after gaining this feat, the bond you made with the fey invokes the power of the First World to return you to life. Immediately after dying, you revive, becoming conscious (and [wounded](/Conditions.aspx?ID=42) as normal) at 27 Hit Points, and you gain the fey trait. Your eyes become a rainbow of colors, and you take on a visual aspect of the fey with whom you are bound, such as by growing wings, horns, or a plantlike body. The change has no mechanical effect; for instance, the wings wouldn't allow you to fly, nor would horns grant a horn unarmed attack.

 The second time you die, you reawaken in the First World with the full appearance of the fey that was bound to you. You become an NPC, unconcerned with your old mortal life. You can be returned to your previous life in the [Material Plane](/Planes.aspx?ID=1) by having allies spend 3 days building a shrine to the First World, giving three offerings that hold deep sentimental value for you or another, and holding a raucous, three-day long feast.

 Any time that you die after that, you reawaken again in the First World with no memories of your previous life, and you can only be brought back by powerful magic such as a [_wish_](/Spells.aspx?ID=377) spell.

</title>

<traits>

---

A flighty breeze follows you wherever you go, granting a dramatic flair to everything you do. You're light on your feet, your voice gains an airy quality that allows it to travel further than normal, and your clothing and hair rustle gently around you at all times. You can Stride at half your land Speed across calm air. If you attempt to carry another creature with you while walking on air, even if it's in an [extradimensional](/Traits.aspx?ID=67) space, you fall.

[Cryptic Spell](/Feats.aspx?ID=3761) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Concentrate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=32" />
<trait label="Druid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=52" />
<trait label="Manipulate" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=104" />
<trait label="Metamagic" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=107" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 64

**Requirements**
You're in natural terrain.

</column>

---

You hide your magic in the croak of a frog, in the sway of the trees, in the howl of the wind, and the flicker of the will-o'-wisp. If the next action you take is to Cast a Spell, attempt a [Nature](/Skills.aspx?ID=10) check against all observers' Perception DCs. If you succeed at your check against an observer's Perception DC, that observer doesn't notice that you're Casting a Spell, even though verbal, somatic, and material components are usually noticeable, and spells normally have sensory manifestations that would make spellcasting obvious to those nearby. All of these are instead hidden in the natural sights and sounds of the environment.

 This ability hides only the spell's spellcasting actions and manifestations, not its effects, so an observer might still see you transform into a giant bear.

<traits>

With a bit of hide, some antlers, and some cast-off fur, you can create a disguise that will fool even an experienced hunter. Impersonating a larger creature doesn't change your actual size.

>
[Can't You See?](/Feats.aspx?ID=3763) <actions string="" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Druid" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=52" />
<trait label="Ranger" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=136" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 64

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11); Expert in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15)

</column>

---

The eye rebels, the mind recoils—no matter how much those who can see you try to explain what's there, their friends' gazes just skitter over you, like a bird afraid to land. A character who attempts to [Point Out](/Actions.aspx?ID=97) your location must attempt a DC 14 flat check. If they fail, their allies misunderstand them and aren't sure where you are. On a critical failure, their allies think they pointed you out in a different location entirely, chosen by the GM. Similarly, when a creature critically fails to [Seek](/Actions.aspx?ID=84) you while you're [hidden](/Conditions.aspx?ID=22) to or [undetected](/Conditions.aspx?ID=39) by it, it thinks you're in a different location chosen by the GM. In either case, you appear to be hidden to a creature that thinks you're in a different location, though you're actually undetected by it for targeting and further uses of the Seek action.
name: Can't You See?
prerequisite: Trained in Occultism; Expert in Stealth

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 65 **Frequency** once per hour **Prerequisites** Expert in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11); Expert in [Survival](/Skills.aspx?ID=16) **Requirements** You must be in either natural terrain or in abandoned or relatively unused artificial terrain (such as a darkened alley or haunted house). --- You know there are places in the world that are just wrong— places where the birds don't sing and where you always feel like you're being watched. You can spot these places, and you can awaken them. To do so, you must gesture toward a 10-foot by 10- foot square you can see and make an ominous proclamation of some manner (i.e. “This is cursed ground,” “That is an ill-omened place.”). The next creature that enters the marked territory must attempt a Will save against your spell DC (if you're a druid) or class DC (if you're a ranger).
**Success** The target is unaffected.
**Failure** Something goes horribly awry for the victim in the cursed ground. The details are up to the GM—it can be a purely “natural” accident (they step into an old bear trap, perhaps) or something stranger and more spectral. The target gains a condition for 2 rounds. Roll 1d4 on the table and use the failure column to determine which condition.
**Critical Failure** As failure, but the effect is astonishingly gruesome. Use the critical failure column, and the condition lasts for 1 minute. ##

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 78 **Frequency** once per hour **Prerequisites** Expert in [Occultism](/Skills.aspx?ID=11) --- You've learned how to read the natural auras of other living creatures. To do this, you must focus on a single living target without blinking for 1 minute. You can do this while performing some other minor task—such as making conversation to distract from your intentions—but you can't blink or otherwise lose your concentration. You can then perceive any or all of the following information.
  • The target's current apparent attitude toward you ([friendly](/Conditions.aspx?ID=18), [indifferent](/Conditions.aspx?ID=25), and so on).
  • The target's current apparent emotional state.
  • A general assessment of the target's physical health, such as what conditions or afflictions it has. You might need to succeed at an Occultism check against the affliction or condition's DC to detect the presence of a specifically hidden or subtle condition or affliction.
In addition, the GM rolls a secret Occultism check for you against the target's [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5) DC. If your result exceeds your target's, you can identify if they're being deceptive in some way (such as expressing a false attitude toward you or faking an emotional state). This doesn't allow you to automatically identify the exact nature of that deception, only to tell the outward appearance is false.
name: Aura Sight

When confronted with the unknown, you can receive knowledge beyond your own experience via written messages delivered by your hand. You spend 10 minutes seated while holding a writing utensil, using it to make small circular motions as you open your mind to the forces around you. At the end of these 10 minutes, [Recall Knowledge](/Actions.aspx?ID=26) with any [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) skill in which you are not trained, using your Occultism modifier instead of your modifier with that skill. VioletYou purify the body, attempting to end persistent poison damage.

---

You know how to stimulate a body's natural healing abilities through the application of resonant crystals. Doing so requires you to use at least two semiprecious stones with a total value of 5 gp or more in place of [healer's tools](/Equipment.aspx?ID=25), which allows you to attempt to [Treat Disease](/Actions.aspx?ID=55) or [Treat Poison](/Actions.aspx?ID=56) using Occultism rather than [Medicine](/Skills.aspx?ID=9). Examples and prices of semiprecious stones can be found under [Gems](/Rules.aspx?ID=1111).

 If you're an expert in Occultism and you use gems whose total value equals or exceeds 50 gp, you gain a +1 item bonus to your Occultism check. If you're a master and the gems' value equals or exceeds 700 gp, the item bonus increases to +2; if you're legendary in Occultism and the gems' value equals or exceeds 15,000 gp, the item bonus increases to +3.

You can find what you're looking for using a dowsing rod or pendulum. Even if the liquid is concealed from you—for example, if it stems from an underground spring or is piped through a wall—this technique points you in the right direction. You've attuned your natural aura to that of plant life, coaxing it to grow faster than normal. You sit for 10 minutes with a small, natural non-creature plant—such as a lone flower, a small bush, or a potted succulent—while you bring your aura in tune through meditation. You coax the plant to advance one stage in its life cycle: from seed to sprout, sprout to plant, plant to flower, or flower to fruit. If the plant doesn't have proper nutrients (if you're sprouting a seed without soil or water, for example), the plant withers 5 minutes after you complete the activity. Performing this activity more than once per day renders you [fatigued](/Conditions.aspx?ID=15) and unable to use Morphic Manipulation until your next full night's rest.

This detects objects with significant emotional resonance attached to them, such as the joy from a child's beloved teddy bear, the sorrow from a widower's wedding ring, or the fear from a victim's murder weapon. If you're looking for a particular type of emotional resonance, you can choose to ignore other emotions. If you find an item with that resonance, you can explore that resonance with the following action.

 **Psychometric Assessment** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32), [divination](/Traits.aspx?ID=47), [emotion](/Traits.aspx?ID=60), [exploration](/Traits.aspx?ID=66), [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106), [occult](/Traits.aspx?ID=120)) **Requirements** Your bare hands are touching an object in which you detected psychometric resonance; **Effect** You spend 1 minute concentrating on the object to get a vision of the face of the person who imbued the item with such emotion in the first place. If the associated emotion is painfully negative, you might take 1d6 psychic damage, as determined by the GM.

    level="1"
    right="Feat 7"
    pfs="Standard"
>
[Skeptic's Defense](/Feats.aspx?ID=3777) <actions string="Reaction" />
</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="General" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=78" />
<trait label="Skill" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=144" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 79

**Frequency**
once per day

**Prerequisites**
Master in [Intimidation](/Skills.aspx?ID=7)

**Trigger**
You are targeted by or are in the area of a [mental](/Traits.aspx?ID=106) spell or effect.

</column>

---

You don't believe in any mental twaddle, and you're certainly not afraid of it. You scoff and verbally refute the triggering effect, attempting a [counteract](/Rules.aspx?ID=371) check using your Intimidation modifier with a counteract level of half your level rounded up. If you succeed, you ignore the triggering effect, though any other creatures that were also targeted or in the area are still affected. If the source of the effect you successfully counteracted understands your language and has an Intelligence modifier of –3 or higher, that creature becomes [stupefied](/Conditions.aspx?ID=37) for 1 round.
name: Skeptic's Defense

An invisible arm extends from you to grab and manipulate objects. The arm reaches up to 15 feet, grabs an unattended object of 1 Bulk or less, and immediately deposits it in one of your free hands or at your feet. Alternatively, it reaches up to 15 feet and performs a simple Interact action like pushing open a window, though it can't perform actions that require significant mechanical dexterity. For every 5 levels you have, the amount the hand can lift increases by 1 Bulk, and the arm's range increases by 15 feet. Being ghostly, the arm can affect [ghosts](/MonsterFamilies.aspx?ID=51), [spirits](/Traits.aspx?ID=149), and other [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) entities, though in most cases, you need an awakening for this to be useful.

>
[Distant Wandering](/Feats.aspx?ID=3791) <actions string="Single Action" />
</title>

<spoilers>May contain spoilers from Gatewalkers</spoilers>

<traits>
<trait label="Rare" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=137" />
<trait label="Deviant" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=426" />

<trait label="Magical" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=103" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Gatewalkers Player's Guide](/Sources.aspx?ID=190) pg. 11, [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 103

</column>

---

Your body falls [unconscious](/Conditions.aspx?ID=38) and your spirit projects out of it. While in spirit form, you can't consciously move your body, and you are [invisible](/Conditions.aspx?ID=26) and inaudible, though a creature still might notice the signs of your presence and passing, just like for an invisible creature affected by [_silence_](/Spells.aspx?ID=287), or a [_prying eye_](/Spells.aspx?ID=239). You can freely move about, though you can't touch or move anything, cast spells, attack, or otherwise affect anything around you. Despite your ghostly form, you are not [incorporeal](/Traits.aspx?ID=222) and can't pass through barriers you couldn't in your body. Most effects can't harm your spirit form, though some spells, like [_spirit blast_](/Spells.aspx?ID=301) and [_spirit song_](/Spells.aspx?ID=303), explicitly damage a creature's spirit. You can return to your body as a free action. If you are in spirit form at the beginning of your turn, you must attempt another backlash check for your deviation, returning to your body if you fail.
name: Distant Wandering

It must succeed at a Will save against the higher of your class DC or spell DC or become frightened 1 (frightened 2 on a critical failure) and be stupefied 1 as long as the frightened condition lasts. Once you've used Warped Reflection against a creature, it's temporarily immune for 24 hours.

</title>

<traits>
<trait label="Uncommon" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=159" />
<trait label="Archetype" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=12" />
<trait label="Dedication" url="/Traits.aspx?ID=41" />
</traits>

<column gap="tiny">

**Source** [Dark Archive](/Sources.aspx?ID=129) pg. 126

**Archetype** [Alter Ego](/Archetypes.aspx?ID=187)

**Prerequisites**
Trained in [Deception](/Skills.aspx?ID=5); Trained in [Stealth](/Skills.aspx?ID=15)

</column>

---

You make yourself into a living mirror, becoming a double of someone unremarkable, and you slip into exactly the role that can get you past security or into a sensitive facility. You become an expert in Deception. You gain the Assume a Role activity.

 **Assume a Role** ([concentrate](/Traits.aspx?ID=32)) **Requirements** You've spent at least 1 hour studying a creature whose role you intend to copy and have done so within the last 3 days. This could include meeting and learning from someone in that role, tailing and spying on someone, using magic to observe them at work, or some other method, as long as you have a visual source of information; **Effect** You quickly and accurately learn how to do mundane jobs or at least copy the movements enough to appear as if you do. A chosen role can take many forms—from cook, cleaner, or librarian to cult member, priest, or duke—but it's always a role and never a specific individual.

 You perform the [Impersonate](/Actions.aspx?ID=46) activity to pass as a member of the role you observed and gain a +1 circumstance bonus to any Deception checks you attempt in your impersonation. This takes the normal amount of time it takes you to Impersonate. You also choose one [Lore](/Skills.aspx?ID=8) skill relevant to that role (such as Farming Lore for a farmer). While in your role, you gain a +1 circumstance bonus to checks for that Lore skill, and if you're untrained in it, you can use your level as your proficiency bonus. You stop assuming the role after 24 hours, if you start studying for a new role, or if you choose to.

**Special** You can't select another dedication feat until you've gained two other feats from the alter ego archetype.

<title level="2">Alter Ego Dedication leads to...</title>
[Borrow Memories](/Feats.aspx?ID=3814), [Change of Face](/Feats.aspx?ID=3808), [Fake It Till You Make it](/Feats.aspx?ID=3809), [Illusory Identity](/Feats.aspx?ID=4149), [In Plain Sight](/Feats.aspx?ID=3810), [It Was Me All Along!](/Feats.aspx?ID=4152), [Muscle Mimicry](/Feats.aspx?ID=3812), [Sound Mirror](/Feats.aspx?ID=3811), [Swap Reflections](/Feats.aspx?ID=3813), [We're on the List](/Feats.aspx?ID=4132)
name: Alter Ego Dedication
